The keyboard moves to that shell from the worker's own session read, which the coordinator's published session can still be behind, so while the close is sending or awaiting its topology an update that lacks the shell, or shows it before its folder is known, keeps the keyboard on it (`Runtime::close_shell_in_flight`) rather than retire it to the tab's focused pane, which is the pane being closed and would hold the keyboard after it is gone.
The context keeps the tab's name apart from the label Hide displays, and whether the operator gave it (`ClosedContext::tab_name`, `Named` against `Labeled`, so a reopened or woken tab is recorded as the operator's again under its new id), and a reopen or a wake that opens a tab sends the engine only that name (`ClosedContext::engine_tab_label`), because the engine keeps any `tab_label` an applied layout carries as the tab's own name; a pane reopened into a tab that still exists sends none, so a rename made after the close stays, and a record saved before the field reads as `Unrecorded` and sends `tab_label` as it always did.
A pane closing beside other panes in its tab stays drawn until the engine confirms it, moving only the keyboard to a surviving pane, because the engine decides the neighbours' geometry.
The captured item is a reservation separate from the twenty confirmed entries, so a failed or unknown close cannot evict older undo history.
A definitive refusal from the engine releases only that reservation; a transport failure or malformed acknowledgement keeps it available, starts one read-only status check, and reports the uncertainty inline.
The status check applies its fresh session snapshot to the navigator before classifying the reservation, so a target confirmed absent cannot remain drawn until another unrelated event arrives.
Only an authoritative absence promotes a reservation into the confirmed LIFO stack, in original user request order; the newest unresolved reservation blocks reopen from silently selecting an older item.
The core's own engine takes the target out of its layout before its close call returns, so that absence can complete a close before the close's own answer arrives; an answer for a close no longer in flight then changes nothing, because the session already settled it and taking the entry back off the stack would leave a reopen waiting for a session the engine has no reason to send again.
A reopen asked for while that newest close is still settling is held (`reopen_after_close`) instead of refused, because its tab has already left the screen: it runs when that close is promoted with a captured item and this machine is in front, and is dropped when the close ends any other way or a newer close starts, so it never reaches an older item.
The snapshot exposes the count, top label, pending reservations, in-flight state, async operation records, and inline notices; the shell routes the menu and shortcut and renders those values without keeping a second stack.
Unknown agent activity is a separate close guard: the core refuses local and remote destructive close until a fresh status is available, while ordinary working or unresolved demand uses the existing one-time confirmation.

A close kept for reopen holds the delivery registration of each agent its panes ran, as a sleeping session's is held (`runtime/closed_registrations.rs`).
`closed_panes` records it on the agent's `ClosedAgent` at the close's start, from the delivery ledger (`delivery_registration_of`), and the close and then its item on the stack hold it, so the pane's absence ends neither the registration nor the watches on it.
While held the agent reads `closed` in `hide agent list`, `hide agent show` and `hide ps` (`coordination::life`), its parent's watch is not read and so warns of no quiet, it holds no place under its mission's or its plan's cap, and its mission reads it as having no worker until it is back.
A letter to it is taken and waits with no bell, as one to a sleeper does, while its hour runs (`closed_target`).
Reopening the item continues each registration whose conversation resumed in the new pane by the wake's own step (`take_over_registration`, then `coordination::rebind` in the delivery store), so its letters, the watch on it, its parent and its spawn receipt follow it, and the lineage worker writes `parent_pane` and the session tokens again from the moved registration.
An agent whose conversation did not resume started a new one there, which is another agent, and its old registration is let go.
A close that settled without an item and an item pushed off the stack let theirs go, to end with the closed pane (`release_dormant_hold`); the stack is memory only, so a restarted core holds nothing and its first read ends them.

A subtree close (`close_tree`, PRD close-agent-subtree) is one event naming the target pane or tab and the descendant panes the sheet showed at the press, and `runtime/tree_close.rs` runs it as one operation made of the ordinary closes above.
Admission happens once, as the event arrives: the listed panes are intersected with the live descendants outside the target, an absent one counts as closed, a pane that now needs a status check or an unconfirmed risky pane refuses the whole close, an ordinary close of a listed pane that ended refused or failed is dismissed as the retry it is (only once the close is admitted, and never one whose replacement shell may already exist), a tab held by something that needs the operator refuses the whole close, and a close with a local node needs at least one free close slot, so a refusal closes nothing.
At most 64 panes per tree and four trees run at once.
The close slots are the ordinary close records, at most `RECENT_CLOSED_LIMIT` at once; an admitted tree holds a fixed number of them for its whole life (`TreeClose::slots`, at most half of what was free at admission, rounded up, so ordinary closes and the next tree keep the rest), and a local node starts only on a slot of its tree that no node occupies.
A node occupies its slot from the moment its close starts until its close record leaves the queue, after the pane is gone, so a tree of any listed size runs through its slots without being refused one halfway, and ordinary closes count only the slots trees hold and do not occupy as taken.
A node waiting for a slot waits while the records holding its tree's slots leave by themselves, and fails at once (`close_queue_unresolved`) when a close that needs the operator holds the queue in front of them, since those slots would then never come back.
Each node starts only when every descendant it waits on is confirmed absent, as a local `close_pane`/`close_tab` through the same capture path (reopen entry included) or as a device's `remote_control` close; the ingest paths and the async-operation tick advance the trees, so nothing waits or blocks under `Mutex<Runtime>`.
A node waits for its tab only while what holds it goes away by itself: a running close or pane operation, or a finished close queued behind a running one; a close that needs the operator (an unknown result, a failed replacement-shell close, a failed pane operation, a device close whose result is unknown) fails it at once, a tab still busy after the pane timeout fails it too, and a device that leaves the status list fails its node rather than reading as a confirmed close.
A refused, timed-out or disconnected node fails itself and every ancestor, which never start, while other branches finish; the tree publishes one `tree.close` async operation per node, the target's with stage `target` and the rest with stage `tree`, all sharing the tree's scope so a surface can count its progress, and writes `tree_close.started`, `tree_close.pane_failed` and `tree_close.finished` diagnostics with the tree and pane ids.
A target's tree (`TreeFinal::Close`) is one Reopen Closed entry, `ClosedItem::Tree` (`runtime/tree_reopen.rs`): each local node's captured item is kept out of the stack as its close settles, and once the tree has finished and every node's close has left the queue one entry holding them, parents before their children, is pushed, so a tree of up to 64 panes takes one of the twenty places and never pushes its own first nodes out.
Each node's close holds its agents' registrations as every kept close does (above), and its captured item keeps holding them while the tree records its entry.
Reopening the entry runs its members one at a time through the ordinary single-item reopen, the target first and the keyboard left there, so each member's registrations are continued in their new panes as any reopened item's are.
A member that does not come back stays in the entry with every member under it, which is skipped, while other branches go on.
While a tree is recording its entry, Reopen Closed is refused with the settling reason rather than reaching an older item.
Delete worktree and Remove project take the same tree as a prelude when the operator chose to close the agents outside: the removal is recorded first, the tree runs, and only a tree with no failure hands over to the ordinary pane close and removal; a failed tree fails the removal with its reason, and a retry lists only what is left.

Recreation also runs outside `Mutex<Runtime>`.
Pane restore uses the captured parent path, direct neighbor, split direction, original first-child ratio, and cwd, falling back to the tab's current pane and then the checkout root when the original facts no longer exist.
A direct pane sibling uses `Engine::split_pane_at`; a sibling subtree is wrapped at its captured nested parent with `Engine::apply_layout`, preserving the surrounding tree and every existing ratio.
Tab restore resolves each captured pane's cwd and label, applies the remaining exported layout, restores its workspace position, and starts each captured agent in the new pane with the captured session id when the agent kind supports resume, followed by the launch choice it was started with (Agent start above); the pane the reopen made keeps that choice for the next restart.
The create, split, and applied-layout requests stamp their panes with a reserved `HIDE_REOPEN_INTENT` environment value containing the closed-item key and mutation stage.
On a retry, the worker adopts only a pane or layout carrying that exact marker; a new id, matching cwd, or matching workspace or tab label is never ownership evidence, so an unrelated agent cannot be interrupted as part of restore.
Both a recovered layout and the first `apply_layout` result must contain the exact expected terminal-pane count before any agent starts.
An under-count is repaired once by reapplying the fully tagged intended layout to the owned tab and revalidating the returned count; an over-count is never adopted or overwritten because the extra pane may have another owner.
The engine's create and split calls carry no operation context, and the request envelope id is correlation only, so this marker is the topology evidence that makes an acknowledged-late mutation converge without guessing.
A layout-only restore can surface an agent process that is still running in the new tab, so the restore worker interrupts it before `Engine::start_agent` applies the explicit resume arguments.
A failure before a pane or tab exists retains the same closed item for retry; once a tab exists, failed agent starts degrade to a shell or fresh session and publish a pane-local notice rather than offering a partial pane retry.
File reads use the filesystem worker, and missing, unreadable, already-open, and successfully reopened files each have an explicit result.
A file close carries its matching debounced save in the same core event, writes that exact path and contents outside the runtime mutex, and removes the tab only after the current draft saves successfully.
No reopen notice uses the shell's modal interaction alert.
A 세션 보관 close (Session archive, below) is a subtree close whose panes never enter this stack (`archive_closes_pane` in `retain_for_reopen`): the archived session has its own way back, 이어가기, and an archived pane that Reopen Closed brought back would be a second live copy of the same conversation.

## Agent sleep

Agent sleep (PRD agent-sleep) ends an agent that has sat seen and untouched past the operator's chosen hours and resumes its conversation when the operator comes back; it exists because the engine has no hibernate of its own.
Seven kinds sleep, as their adapters declare (`hide-agent-adapter/src/declarations.rs`): Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity sleep in their pane, and Grok, OpenCode, Pi and omp close their pane and keep a dormant record (below).
The hours are Settings' choice of 12, 24, 48 or 72, or Off, and 24 until the operator chooses (`agent_sleep::DEFAULT_SLEEP_AFTER_HOURS`).
`core-state.json` writes an Off the operator chose as 0 (`agent_sleep::stored_after_hours`) and loads no value, or a value that is not a choice, as 24 (`loaded_after_hours`): a store written while Off was the default wrote null for both, so it now sleeps after 24 hours, and a build from before the 24-hour default loads 0, which is none of its choices, as Off.
Besides the hours, an agent sleeps when its mission node finishes, when `hide agent sleep` asks for it, and from the pane menu; a letter that needs an answer wakes it (Sleep by mission, letter and command, below).
Three owners keep it replaceable when the engine gains one (D-20): `hide-core/src/agent_sleep.rs` decides and remembers and makes no call, `hide-core/src/agent_sleep_engine.rs` is the one module that touches the engine and processes, and `hide-core/src/runtime/agent_sleep.rs` connects them to the runtime.
The local coordinator's tick runs the decision at most once a minute; a tick inside the minute is one integer comparison, and the minute pass reads the agent rows and makes no call under the lock.
Each decided end runs on its own worker, at most four at once: it reads the agent again from the engine and refuses unless it is still idle or done and the same kind, so a sleep is never decided on a turn, and it goes on only when the engine's process facts (`Engine::pane_processes`) name a foreground group that is not the shell's.
It first presses the agent's own quit key and waits up to five seconds for the shell to hold the terminal: an agent that quits on its own puts back the terminal modes it set, as the operator's quit does, and no signal makes one do so (Codex CLI 0.165.0 ended by SIGHUP, SIGINT or SIGTERM leaves its keyboard protocol, alternate screen and mouse reports on).
The key is the sleep dialect's declaration (`LaunchDialect::quit_key`: Ctrl+C for Claude Code, Codex CLI and agy), and the core names no agent; Ctrl+D is never pressed, because a shell that already holds the terminal ends on it.
The key is pressed again only on what the agent shows after a press, read from the pane every 100 ms (`agent_sleep_engine::Quit`): the hint it shows while it waits for the key a second time (`LaunchDialect::quit_again`: Claude Code's "Press Ctrl-C again to exit", agy's "press ctrl+c again to exit"), or its composer, judged by its composer declaration, emptied of a draft the press cleared; at most three presses.
Codex CLI 0.165.0 quits on the first press into an empty composer, and a second press sent at a fixed 150 ms reached it while it was already quitting and was left for the shell to read, in the keyboard protocol Codex had turned on (`ESC[99;5u`, shown by zsh as `9;5u` in front of the wake's resume line, with-hide/hide-private#37).
The wake clears nothing from that line before it types the resume line, so what the line still holds runs in front of it: a quit key the agent never read before the node ended it below, which comes only after `agent_sleep.exit_keys_unanswered`, or a terminal's answer to a query the agent made that arrives after it exited, which no run has shown.
A turn that started between the read and the press is interrupted by it, as the end below would have ended it.
An agent still running then is ended by the pane's node (`terminate_group`, which the node refuses for a group of 1 or less, logged as `agent_sleep.exit_keys_unanswered` with the presses sent first), and the worker waits up to ten seconds more for the shell to hold the terminal.
That end leaves the agent's terminal modes in the pane: the pane's terminal follows its modes from what the pane prints and resets none when the shell takes the terminal back, so the alternate screen and mouse reports stay on in every view (Hide's view sends the operator's keys as typed, and xterm.js 6 has no keyboard protocol).
The node answers what the end did (`GroupEnd`): a job that ended on its own since the last look is `gone`, and a process under a Windows leader that was left running is named with why and logged as `agent_sleep.end_left_running`; neither fails the sleep, which waits for the shell either way (`an_end_that_finds_the_agent_gone_or_leaves_a_process_still_sleeps_it`).
On Unix that end is SIGTERM to the process group, and it never escalates to SIGKILL.
Windows keeps no process group: the platform layer names the process the shell runs now as the group (and the shell again once none is left, `hide_platform::process::console_foreground`), so the node ends that process and every process under it, at once, because no polite signal reaches a process on another console (The platform layer below).
An agent ended that way on Windows cannot put back its terminal modes, and that is a known gap ([INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md#what-each-system-supports)): a Windows prompt reads a bracketed paste an agent left on as keys, and Herdr wrapping the line it typed in that paste was the known cause there ([herdrdev/herdr#5371](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/issues/5371)); the core's own engine types the wake's start line as bytes, unwrapped (`type_agent_start`), and the gap stays listed until a wake measured after a forced end on Windows shows the line running.
A Unix shell is not caught by it: zsh and bash read bracketed paste and set the mode themselves at each prompt.
A refused or timed-out end leaves the agent awake and the pane alone for an hour or until its state changes.
The engine then drops the agent from its session with its session reference and answers a prompt to the pane with `agent_not_found`, so nothing reaches the shell and nothing guards against it; the sleep record, persisted in `core-state.json` beside the read records and off the wire, is what draws the row until an agent is back.
A wake first renews the pane's holder when an earlier build started it, and types nothing when afterwards no holder is known to run the pane ([The pane holder](#the-pane-holder)); then it is the engine's own start (`Engine::start_agent`) in the same pane, under the agent's name when it had one (orchestrators address agents by name) or `wake-<pane>` otherwise, with the provider's resume arguments from `recent_closed::resume_arguments`, or none for Start new session, followed by the launch choice the sleep record kept from the agent (Agent start above).
A committed visit that changes the tab on screen, Wake agent and Retry resume; a wake asked for while the end is in flight runs when it lands; a second wake while one runs starts nothing.
A wake asked for before the pane's engine has finished its restore (the first visit after this daemon or a device's link started) reads waking while it waits for that restore, as every start does (Agent start above), and runs once it lands.
A failed wake's `reason` is an `agent_wake.*` code (`folder_missing`, `not_resumed`, `not_started`, `not_ready`, `launch_choice_refused`; `agent_sleep_engine::WAKE_*`) that `web/src/startReason.ts` words, and the folder and the engine's code and message stay in the `agent_sleep.wake_failed` diagnostic.
The engine answers the start once it has typed the start line, so a wake whose agent has not appeared in its pane by the start's deadline (`AGENT_START_DEADLINE`, 120 s, read at the next minute's tick) fails the same way with `agent_wake.not_ready`, rather than reading waking for good (`a_wake_whose_agent_never_appears_fails_at_the_starts_deadline`).
The last look is stamped when a visit commits and once a minute while a pane is in the tab on screen, and the stamps are saved through the coalesced state save, never published.
The hours count from the later of the agent's last conversation line and its last look (`PaneStamps::idle_since`).
The last conversation line is the newest request or reply the session read proves (`last_conversation_at_unix_ms`), because a relaunch or an engine restart reports a state for a moment and moves the change stamp without adding a line to the conversation; on 2026-10-22 one app update restarted every idle agent's 24 hours that way.
Until a session read proves a line, the change stamp stands in, so a restart only ever delays a sleep.
A pane's stamp, and the last look in it, is dropped only when the engine's topology no longer holds the pane, never because the agent list holds no agent for it: a restarted engine lists an agent only once its program shows again, and a stamp lost in that gap sleeps an agent the operator just read the moment the session read proves its old conversation (`AgentSleepStore::stamp`; the read records follow the same rule, `prune_read_records`).
A wake stamps a last look, as a visit does, because the conversation it resumes is as old as the sleep and would make the agent due again at the next minute.
A relaunch forgets an end that was in flight, because it cannot know whether it landed, and reads a wake that was in flight as still asleep until an agent appears in the pane.
An in-pane sleep keeps the read axis's engine mark beside the ended agent's state sequence: the sequence identifies the ended agent only on that engine, because an engine restart starts its counter again.
A listed provider whose program has shown wakes the record when either the sequence or that mark differs; a pane with no mark uses its read connection's, and an older record with no mark cannot claim that a newly listed agent is still the ended one.

### Sleep by mission, letter and command

PRD mission-worker-sleep puts a finished mission's agents to sleep early and lets letters reach them asleep; `hide-core/src/runtime/agent_sleep/{missions,letters,command}.rs` own the three, and every end and wake is the ones above.
A mission node finishes for its agents when its status becomes done or dropped, however it got there, when every pull request it holds is read merged or closed, or when its mission closes (done, cancelled, or a merge wait that settled).
Every save of the mission book compares the finished nodes with the last save's (`note_mission_finishes`), so no path that changes the book needs its own call; a node that finished marks its worker and the checkers bound to its lines, never the Conductor, and a node opened again (a defect, changes asked for, a status set back to working) drops its marks.
The book read at start is the first comparison, so a restart marks nothing for a finish it already saw; the marks are memory only, and a restart leaves an unslept mark to the hours rule.
A plan's handed step marks its child the same way when it becomes done or is taken back (`SleepMark::plan`, PRD hide-plan-delegate B18); the mission book's comparison leaves those marks alone.
The minute decision ends each marked agent by the pane menu's rules, with the operator's screen added and the time and the seen state left out, within the four ends in flight that every sleep shares; an agent that works, asks the operator, cannot be read or is on screen keeps its mark for the next minute, and one that can never sleep here (its kind, no conversation, another session now in the pane) loses it.
A mark is spent only when its end lands (`mission_sleep_landed`); a refused end keeps it and tries again the next minute without the hour's backoff, and a worker woken after it slept is not put to sleep again for the same finish.
Sleep set to Off clears the marks and sleeps nothing; it is on, at 24 hours, until the operator turns it off, so a finished node's agents sleep by default.

A letter to a registered agent Hide put to sleep is taken, not refused with `target_unavailable`: `prepare_delivery` resolves a target that no live observation answers to the registration whose pane holds an in-pane sleep record for the same session, or whose id a dormant record holds (`sleeping_target`), and the store's commit accepts that target (`delivery_recipient_current`).
The doorbell holds such a letter as absent until the agent is back, and the store's pass reads the asleep recipients from the sleep records under the lock (`delivery_asleep`, a few records, never the ledger), skips their letters' deadlines, and when one wakes takes its sleep out of their waits once (`Ledger::resume_woken`), so no letter turns undelivered for having waited on a sleeper and the ledger's format does not change.
A sleeper whose wake failed is not asleep for the store: nothing will wake it, so its letters' hour runs again from the failure, and a wake that can never start (a terminal the engine could not restore, a pane with no connection) leaves a new request to expire after its hour with no note to its sender, since only a wake that ran and failed tells the sender.
A pending `request` or `block` letter to a sleeping or failed sleeper queues one resume wake in the order such letters arrived; at most four in-pane letter wakes run at once, a dormant one also needs a free dormant transition, and a sleeper already waking or ending is not asked twice.
A `request` or `block` letter wakes its recipient once: one whose bell already rang, or whose wake started before the current sleep, wakes no one and its hour runs through that sleep as it would for an awake agent (`Sleeper::pausing`), so a letter nobody takes in neither wakes the agent after each sleep (by the hours, by its mission or by `hide agent sleep`) nor waits for it forever; the letters that woke someone, with when, are memory beside the queue (`delivery_wakes_started`), so a restart lets each pending one wake once more.
The queue is memory beside the records and the ledger and is rebuilt from them, so a restart queues again what still waits; it moves on a flag the ledger's publish and each sleep transition set, read by the coordinator's 250 ms tick, and the minute decision sets the flag as a fallback.
A letter wake moves nothing on the operator's screen: the in-pane wake starts the agent where it was, and a dormant one opens its tab unfocused.
A dormant wake refused for a passing reason (its checkout busy with another agent operation, no free transition, a close not yet confirmed) stays queued; any other refusal fails its letters as a failed wake does.
Like every wake, a letter wake counts as a look, so a completion the agent finished before it slept no longer reads unread once a letter wakes it; the mission's Conductor and map still carry it (PRD mission-worker-sleep, Risks).
An in-pane letter wake refused before it typed anything, for a cause that passes on its own, is queued again instead (`WakeOutcome::Failed::passing`, the codes `agent_sleep_engine::passes` names): a pane's node that could not take the input now (`pane_input_unavailable`, `pane_input_limit`, `pane_input_cancelled`, as for a device pane no screen attached, `node_busy`), a program that still held the pane's terminal past the start's wait (`agent_pane_busy`), another change of the pane's holder that held its turn (`holder_renewal_busy`), a shell its node could not read (`agent_start.shell_unreadable`), or a renewal whose answer the link lost; it starts again after 5 seconds, then 10, the waits of a refused bell, at most three letter wakes of the sleeper in a row as a letter has three bells (`LetterWakes::tries`, memory beside the queue, forgotten when the agent is back or its letters fail; a wait's end brings the tick's pass as the flag does, once), so a passing refusal no longer fails the letters at once, and the third wake refused for a passing cause fails them for good (with-hide/hide-private#660, #675).
A wake that may have typed its start (the engine's answer lost, an agent that did not appear by the deadline) or was refused for a cause the same wake meets again (its folder, its profile, its launch choice, no resume arguments, a name another agent holds, a pane with no holder, a shell that had not finished starting in the start's wait or waits in its startup files for a key, a start line too long to check) is not tried again, since a second start could start the agent twice or fail the same way.
A wake that fails for good leaves the `request` and `block` letters waiting on it undelivered (`Ledger::fail_undeliverable`, through the store's upkeep), which ends their senders' waits, and the sender gets a `progress` letter from Hide's `hide:wake` identity naming the recipient and the reason, sent `--now` so a sender that works reads it at its next tool call (`WAKE_FAILED_NOTE`); that letter goes out on its own thread and is memory only, so a restart between the two loses it, as does a sender no pane and no sleep record holds any more, which is logged as `agent_sleep.wake_note_unsent`, while the letter's undelivered state stays in the ledger and the reason in the `agent_sleep.letter_wake_failed` diagnostic.
A letter held as `session_unread` because the recipient's session read refused for a reason reading again cannot clear stays pending, and its sender gets one `progress` letter from `hide:delivery` (`runtime/unreadable_letters.rs`, run on the coordinator's tick only after a ledger publish or a pane's refusal moved); the refusal is the labels worker's, kept per pane for the session it was read under and laid on the overlay (`LabelOverlay::refusal`), and the delivery observation carries it as `unreadable` while the turn is unread, so the row's connection mark and the mission banner read the same fact ([delivery.md](delivery.md#letters-while-the-agent-works)).
A later `request` or `block` tries the wake again.

`hide agent sleep <id> [--actor <id>]` runs under the lock like a mission command (`agent_sleep_command`), because the end it starts is the runtime's: the agent itself or its parent may ask, as for `hide agent end`; the pane menu's rules and the operator's screen decide, and a refusal returns its code and next action instead of the menu's error line; asking again while it ends or sleeps answers `ending` or `asleep`.

The panes of every other machine sleep as the core's own do (PRD core-host-node-remote-core B13), whichever way its link was made: a node that dials the core (A core on another machine) and a device the core dials, over SSH or as a WSL distribution, alike, on macOS, Linux and Windows (`SleepMachine::Node`).
The device was left out at first because a wake could start an agent only through the core's own Herdr connection; the core's own engine now runs every machine's panes, and a device's engine starts an agent in its pane (`Engine::start_agent`, as `hide agent spawn --machine` does), and its node ends a process group (`Call::TerminateGroup`), so nothing an in-pane sleep does is the core's machine's alone.
That machine's coordinator's tick runs the same minute decision for its panes, with its own minute; the four ends in flight are counted over every machine.
The records and stamps keep the machine's pane under its `remote:<device>:pane:` id, and each machine's session settles only its own (`SleepScope`): its records are settled against its session as its engine names the panes, before the session is scoped to the device, and its rows are marked and stamped when the core takes that session.
An end or a wake for its pane runs on its engine connection and its link (`SleepTarget`, `InboundLink`, which asks `Runtime::node_link` at each call), with the pane id its engine knows; the agent's name comes from the row's `given_name`, because a device row's `id` is the core's own.
A visit is that machine's tab coming on screen while it is in front, which the core sees in its next session: the tabs that came on screen wake, and the last look of those and of the tabs that left is stamped.
Removing the device forgets its records and stamps; its panes are not touched.
A machine that is not connected neither sleeps nor wakes anything, and nothing waits on its link: the minute decision passes it by, Sleep agent and `hide agent sleep` are refused at once as on a core with no engine (`pane.control_unavailable`, `agent_sleep_unreachable`), a Wake starts nothing and leaves the record asleep (its pane shows the device's `연결 안 됨` in place of the sleep body, so it offers no Wake), and a letter's wake waits in its queue for the connection; an end or a wake already running when the link drops ends within its own bounds (each engine call's five seconds, the start's deadline) and leaves the agent awake or the wake failed with Retry (`a_disconnected_devices_agent_neither_sleeps_nor_wakes_and_nothing_waits`).
A sleep that closes its pane (Grok, OpenCode, Pi, omp) is refused on any machine but the core's (`core_machine_only`), because the dormant record reopens it from the core machine's catalog.

A provider whose implemented sleep dialect declares `closes_pane_when_sleeping` uses a separate dormant conversation record under the same persisted `agent_sleep` store.
The common mechanism does not grant a provider sleep support; its adapter must declare an implemented reader and resume dialect first.
The record's `SleepId` names the durable intent, while the captured native session, node, connection generation and execution sequence fence the old execution.
The existing coalesced state writer acknowledges the exact record only after private atomic replacement and persistence barriers; a failed or stale write cannot authorize a close or start.
Close admission reuses the existing geometry reservation and capture owner, saves the bound close key before sending its effect, and waits for authoritative disappearance before publishing a sleeping row.
A sleep whose end lands after the engine stopped listing the agent asks for the pane's machine's session again (`Runtime::request_republish` for this machine, that device's session sync's `RepublishWaker` for another), since the session that dropped the agent was applied while the record was still ending, which draws no row, and the engine publishes again only on a change; it drops an agent the moment its process ends.
The captured close carries an immutable non-reopenable purpose through its worker replies, so a dormant conversation has only its SleepId wake route and never enters ordinary Reopen Closed.
After that reservation retires, a late sleep capture or close reply cannot recreate an ordinary close operation.
The archive holds at most 256 conversations and four pending or uncertain transitions; a full archive or transition budget refuses admission without closing a pane.
An uncertain result retains its admission and offers explicit status inspection, with at most one inspection worker and a bounded intent-marker scan.
A recovered intent with no saved close key sent no close and is released by that status action without a pane effect.
A wake saves the intent before creating its separate tab, saves the owned tab before starting the provider with the saved native session and cwd, and clears the archive only after current reader facts confirm that conversation in that tab.
The record keeps its checkout's owner as the project list names it when the session sleeps (`DormantOwner`: the repository's main worktree or the plain folder, whether it is a git checkout, and the name a workspace opened for it takes), and the wake opens the checkout from that owner rather than from the list.
The list may not show the checkout then: a linked worktree with no open workspace is listed only once a window has read its repository, which no window may have done since hided started when the Wake comes from a phone, and an unregistered project is listed only while one of its workspaces is open.
A record an older build saved has no owner, so its wake finds the checkout in the list as before.
A Wake on a session whose project the operator removed opens its checkout and lists the project again, by decision: pressing Wake on that session is the operator asking for it.
The row hides Wake for every lasting reason a wake would be refused, and one function (`dormant_wake_blocker`) decides both: a missing reader, an invalid record, another machine's record, no engine connection or, for a record with no owner, an unlisted checkout hides it and says why, while a failed wake keeps the reason it failed; a spent transition budget or a busy checkout passes and keeps Wake.
Its stable intent marker permits reuse of only its own tab; no pane address, input or terminal capability is copied into the new execution.
A session that held a delivery registration when its pane closed saves that registration (its id and the execution that held it) in the same record, from the delivery ledger at admission, and the wake continues it; the core started the wake, so it knows which registration the new pane takes over and nothing is matched by name or guessed afterwards.
While the record holds a registration, the closed pane's absence ends neither the registration nor the watches on it: `observe_registration_panes` queues no end for it and the watch readings do not call its target gone, so letters sent to it stay pending instead of failing with `target_unavailable`.
The wake starts the agent under the name the registration was made with, waiting out the engine's release of the closed agent's name (`agent_start::start_at_shell_reusing_name`); a session with no registration is named as a fork.
An agent whose CLI runs no session hook on resume (`LaunchDialect::resume_reports_session` is false: Cursor, whose `sessionStart` hook is the engine's only source for its session and does not run on `--resume`, issue 938) would leave the woken pane with no session in the engine, so no reader fact, no observed session and no lineage token could ever confirm it.
For such an agent the wake worker, once the engine has started the agent, says which session the pane resumed with `Engine::report_agent_session`, under the source the hook integration uses (`herdr:<kind>`) and a nanosecond sequence, which is exactly what the missing hook would have sent; everything after it is the ordinary confirmation below.
The report is fenced on the saved wake intent like every other write of the worker; a report the engine refuses ends the wake as `WakeUnknown` with `agent_sleep.session_report_failed` logged, and nothing is sent again.
The report names only the id the core resumed; when the engine later has another session for the pane (the agent's own hook after a new chat, which carries a later sequence from the same source), the engine's record wins, the pane's `child_session` token stops matching and the relationship ends as for any pane that hosts another session, while the registration stays with the pane.
Once current reader facts confirm the saved conversation in the wake pane and the pane's observed execution is the same native session, kind and device, the runtime queues a `coordination::Rebind` and keeps the record, and its sleeping row is withdrawn; the delivery store's next pass moves the registration, its letters, its watch and its spawn receipt to the new pane in one transaction, and the lineage writer then writes the parent tokens there because its reconciliation key includes where each registration's pane is.
The record is cleared only after the published ledger shows the move.
A woken pane that is another conversation, kind or device, a registration the operator ended meanwhile, or a pane another registration already holds is not continued: `agent_sleep.registration_refused` is logged with the reason, the hold is released and the registration ends as any whose pane is gone.
Restart converts pending work to Unknown and never resends creation, close or start automatically.
These transitions live in the `dormant` child modules of the same three sleep owners, and all persistence, engine and folder I/O stays off `Mutex<Runtime>`.
Earlier Factory-bound sleeping-session records remain readable.
Their legacy metadata starts no engine, and confirmed ordinary wakes release their saved intent.

The directory-chain barrier is the platform layer's on every system (The platform layer, below); a chain whose barrier fails refuses dormant persistence rather than returning a durability receipt.
The chain is a fact about the state folder, not about one save, so the core makes it durable once per folder per process, by the folder's file identity, and again only for a folder replaced since (`persistence::establish_folder_once`); every save still flushes its file and that file's folder.

## Session archive

세션 보관 (PRD session-archive) closes a root session and every descendant pane with it and keeps the conversations, so the task list stops showing work the operator is done with and 이어가기 brings the whole tree back later.
Two owners keep it apart from sleep: `hide-core/src/session_archive.rs` holds the records (types, the load filter, the cap) and makes no call, and `hide-core/src/runtime/session_archive.rs` drives admission, the close, resume, delete and the rows.
The records live beside the dormant records in `core-state.json` (`session_archive`) with an admission target of 256 sessions, each member counting and deletes still awaiting their receipts discounted.
An archive that would cross the cap makes room from the oldest records at rest, a whole record at a time, before it is admitted (`SessionArchive::admit`, operator decision 2026-11-11, replacing PRD session-archive B12's refusal): a record is at rest when it is archived whole, every member closed and none resumed or being resumed, and no delete is out for it; a failed resume that made no pane is at rest.
A record still saving or closing, one whose close failed or is unknown, the record of an agent end whose pane has not left yet, and a record holding a session that conducts, works or checks an open mission or holds a plan that still waits are never picked, since the delete would take that mission or plan with it; a record whose delete is already out counts for nothing.
Each record picked leaves through the archive's own delete (`Runtime::send_archive_deletes`, below), logged as `session_archive.evicted`; if its deletes cannot be enqueued together, admission is rolled back with `session_archive.eviction_failed` and an archive-save failure, preserving the cap.
Automatic eviction selects nothing until the plan book is Ready and the mission store has been installed with a readable book; a loading or failed restore refuses an admission needing eviction as `archive.full` (`archive_full` for agent end), with `session_archive.eviction_unavailable` naming the unavailable book.
A delete that fails after enqueue keeps its archive record, as manual delete does, and can leave the count above 256 by the sessions whose evictions failed; the next admission selects enough oldest eligible roots to remove that excess as well as make room for its incoming record.
If the link worker deleted the rows but the state writer then failed, the archive record remains with its link rows gone, the existing manual-delete limit; the record remains at rest and can be evicted again through the idempotent delete.
When what is eligible cannot make enough room, the archive is refused before anything closes (`archive.full`).
An automatic descendant waits while its root's accepted start still has a valid screen move pending; consuming, cancelling or expiring that move releases the shared start slot, using the same latest-navigation, connection-generation and 90-second bound as the catalog follow.
A record names its device, project root and checkout, and for each member the machine, pane, kind, native session, source reference, cwd, title, last line, pull requests, the delivery registration it held, its parent and depth.
A load drops a record that does not parse rather than refusing the file, keeps the newest records when the file holds more than the cap (as a restart between an admission and the delete it started can leave it), and a record being deleted is never written again.
A core move carries each member's machine, pane, resumed pane and held registration with the machine it names (`node_migration::KEYS`), and its folders stay beside that machine id.

Admission is one event, `archive_session`, with the root pane and whether the operator confirmed stopping running work; the tree is the root's lineage children and the close descendants the close sheet would list.
A child, Hide AI's own agents, an agent whose conversation Hide has not seen, a device that is not connected and an agent whose activity is unknown are refused with their own kinds; pressing it again on a session already being archived converges on the same record.
The save comes first: the record is written through the coalesced state writer, and only its receipt (`ingest_archive_saved`) starts the close, so a save that fails closes nothing (`archive.save_failed`).
The close is the subtree close (`tree_close.rs`, `TreeFinal::Archive`), local panes and a device's alike; a member counts as closed once its pane is gone, including on a connected device.
A partial close keeps the record as `CloseFailed`: the members that closed stay archived and the live root's record lists them with their own 이어가기 (B24), the notice says once why (refused, timed out, or the device disconnected: `archive.incomplete`, `archive.incomplete_timeout`, `archive.incomplete_disconnected`), and 세션 보관 again converges on the same record; a retry whose save fails leaves the record as it was, the open root at its head.
Once that live root is gone some other way, read from a fresh read of its machine (below) and with neither its pane, a pane its resume made, nor its conversation live, the record stands in `보관됨` itself, as does one whose root resumed and then closed with a member still archived, so a saved conversation never lacks a row.
A tree larger than one subtree close takes (64 panes) is refused before anything is saved (`archive.too_many`).
`hide agent end` (`hide-core/src/coordination/end.rs`, [delivery.md](delivery.md)) keeps the conversation of the pane it closes as a record of its own, one member holding no registration since the registration has ended, admitted before the engine closes the pane and taken back when a close that failed left the pane running (`Runtime::archive_ended`, `Runtime::withdraw_ended`); the session the agent registered with, which its row shows, proves the conversation when the label reader has not confirmed its session file yet, as for an agent ended right after its first turn, and the resume confirms the session by id and folder; a conversation already archived converges on its record, a full archive makes room from its oldest record at rest as any admission does, and an archive whose eligible roots cannot make enough room keeps nothing (`archive_full` in the answer, `agent.end_not_archived` in the log); the archive's refusal is typed (`AdmitRefusal`), so only a full archive reads as full.
That member counts as closed once its pane is gone from its machine's listing, as an archive close's member does, so the listing that still shows the closed pane until that machine's next read is never taken for a resume; the row stands in `보관됨` at once, and its 이어가기 starts once the member closed.
A restart reads a save or close in flight as `CloseUnknown`, and a resume in flight as unknown, keeping the pane it made; `archive_check` settles only those, and only once every member's machine is connected, its panes have been read since (`delivery_panes`) and, for a device, its session is loaded, because before that every pane would look closed; nothing is resent on its own, and a resume is refused while the close is unknown (`archive.close_unknown`).

이어가기 (`archive_resume`, the whole record or one member) runs the members one at a time through the task-operation slot, root first, each through the checkout start (`start_in_checkout`) under the request `archive:<id>:<session>` with the provider's resume arguments for the saved native session; the tab starts in the folder the conversation ran in when that folder is inside the checkout, since a CLI may find its conversations by folder; the tab worker asks that machine's node whether the folder is still there (`Call::Directory`, off the lock) and, as a wake does, refuses a folder that is gone with that reason rather than starting the conversation somewhere it did not run; a start behind the screen does not become the operator's remembered agent choice.
The root takes the screen as an ordinary start does; a descendant starts as a phone start does (`stay_behind`): its tab is created without focus (`CheckoutTabRequest::focus`) and its start moves nothing (`TaskOperation::stays_behind`), because only the operator's pane moves the screen and the engine would otherwise bring the new tab forward and have the core follow it.
A group-qualified creation starts without engine focus; once its selected target is accepted, the core uses the ordinary ordered pane-focus control to bring it forward.
The tab worker rechecks its connection and target while holding the result-publication lock, so a server replaced during creation cannot publish its pane or queue a new focus on the replacement.
A focus already accepted before a later connection change retains the control lane's existing retirement boundary.
The global agent-start panel reads that result without issuing a second pane-focus intent, so a result left behind stays behind in the shell too.
For a connected device, or a local start or new worktree whose returned pane is neither in its checkout's catalog nor drawn ahead there, the current start may hold one follow for at most 90 seconds until its exact pane appears in that checkout's catalog, then sends one ordinary pane focus with device forwarding.
When the start answer names a final tab, both immediate focus and that follow require the pane in that tab; an older catalog that still places an added pane in its temporary staging tab cannot consume the follow or move the visible tab.
The task captures this navigation permission before checkout preparation.
For the first local project, the catalog choosing its first checkout is a fallback rather than a user visit; it retains that permission while the control-lane serial is unchanged and no explicit navigation has cancelled it.
A start result that arrives before its returned pane's catalog waits on that same follow, including when its empty registration row or only its owner's seed pane is already listed, so the checkout and its pane are chosen together rather than focusing a pane while reconciliation still reads the previous checkout.
An accepted local result uses the same local device forwarding as an accepted pane press, including when a remote device was in front.
An intervening local or remote visit, a replacement task or a changed device connection cancels that follow; repeated catalog answers cannot focus it again.
A global start, including an archived root, may open another checkout while its original checkout, group, tab and control-lane focus serial remain current; a later explicit visit cancels that permission even if the operator returns to the same empty group or draft without sending the engine a focus command.
Its reservation keeps the prior area, active tab and delegated canvas until the result; an explicitly targeted start instead keeps the chosen slot, so snapshot synchronization with the old pane cannot cancel a global start.
Only a newly filled slot is selected ahead of topology; an already settled retry follows its pane's current location even after a group move or dissolve.
A retry reuses the pane the earlier attempt made instead of opening another.
A member is done once any live row on its machine shows the same kind and native session, which also covers the operator resuming it by hand; a failed member keeps its reason and its own 이어가기, and the record goes once every member is back.
A member's delivery registration is held while it is archived (`held_registrations`, `archive_holds_actor`): its pane's absence ends neither the registration nor the watches on it, and the resume continues it as a wake does (`continue_dormant_registration`); a resumed pane that closes first, or that the delivery store has not seen within the hour a woken sleeper gets, lets the registration go (`session_archive.registration_released`), and a record that is deleted or pruned releases the holds of its members, leaving a move to a resumed pane already asked to finish.
Deleting (`archive_delete`, or an eviction that makes room, above) removes the record and asks the link worker to delete those sessions' lines (`Runtime::send_archive_deletes`, the one delete both start); the agent's own conversation file is never touched, and no resume starts while that delete is out.
The delete is confirmed by the worker's answer (`deleted`); a failed delete keeps the record (`archive.delete_failed`).

The snapshot publishes `navigator.archived_sessions` (each record's phase, whether it stands in `보관됨` or under a live root, its members' resume state and pull requests).
Both are optional fields, so the protocol's version did not move: an older device daemon or phone reads the snapshot as before and simply offers no archive.
Persistence uses the folder barrier the dormant records use, on every system (The platform layer); the Windows check lane runs `an_archived_session_saves_through_the_folders_barrier_and_loads_back`.

## Conductor missions

A Conductor's mission (PRD software-factory-conductor) is a core-owned record, `hide-core/src/missions.rs` for the model, `mission_store.rs` for its files and `runtime/missions.rs` for the commands, admissions and wakes; the Conductor's own judgement (what to start, retry or ask) stays in its conversation, and the record holds only what the map shows and the contracts Hide enforces: one Conductor per mission, no worker before the plan is approved, a worker only on the project's machine, and the mission's cap.
Each `hide mission` command is one typed event applied under `Mutex<Runtime>` ([delivery.md: Missions](delivery.md#missions)).
Each mission is saved alone in `state/missions/<id>.json`, a schema-4 book of one mission, with `missions/index.json` holding the next id and one metadata line per mission (`hide_kit::layout::{missions_dir,mission_file,mission_index}`).
`mission_events::MissionEventStore` owns the one writer, saves histories before their missions, atomically replaces private files through `hide-platform::fs`, rewrites only bodies whose encoded bytes changed before their index lines, and rewrites the index only when a line changed.
The old 128-mission admission and load limit is gone; each mission still has at most 64 nodes and its own 7 MiB write budget below its 8 MiB read cap.
The runtime holds every open mission, every closed mission still asking someone, and the newest 128 other closed bodies and histories; older closed missions keep only their metadata in memory, with their files intact.
The shelf retains at most 2,048 older closed records; excess records lose their oldest closed row, body and owned history after the new index commits, with a diagnostic.
Startup streams index rows, retaining only the newest 128 + 2,048 resting closed rows before reading bodies; open or still-asking rows are retained.
The writer retains at most 32 unsaved shelved bodies and their histories, counted across its queue and active write until the book and histories are durable.
At 32, creation returns `mission_save_pending` with a storage-retry message and a diagnostic; existing live missions may still close and stay loaded until shelving can resume, preserving unsaved data.
The ordinary loaded body/history bound is open or still-asking work plus 128, with at most 32 pending shelves; existing live bodies retained during storage failure are not discarded.
The CLI list includes shelved metadata, filtered by project and device, with `shelved: true`; explicit `show` and `reopen` read one body off the runtime lock after preceding saves finish, with reopen also restoring its history and enforcing the existing Conductor, cancellation and open-mission checks.
The first migration can temporarily retain additional legacy closed bodies while the 32-slot writer drains; that source book retains its existing 8 MiB read cap, and later saves or a restart finish shelving.
No body cache is kept: snapshots, Missions screens, chips, saved map cards, cost attribution and PR-driven reopening consume only loaded bodies.
With no index, launch reads the old schema-4 `missions.json` (`hide_kit::layout::missions`), preserving the existing schema-1/2/3 conversions and first-copy backups; the first save writes all bodies before installing the index, so a partial failure leaves the old file authoritative on the next start.
The old file is retained and never updated by this store: a downgrade sees the missions at migration, and a later upgrade uses the existing index and ignores changes the downgraded build wrote to `missions.json`.
An unreadable index is never replaced and mission commands answer `mission_unavailable`; an unreadable body is logged and left on disk, retaining its line for explicit access.
The mission folder, including its index, and the legacy book move with the core to another machine (`node_migration::MOVES_WITH_CORE`): a move maps each mission's machine, Project registration (`workspace_id`) and Conductor's pane and session machine as it maps the ledger's (`node_migration::KEYS`, `reown`), and keeps its paths, which sit beside its machine.
It is published as its own revisioned rest section, `missions`, made on the snapshot read (`refresh_missions`): with no mission that read does nothing, and otherwise it compares the book's change count, the count of pull request answers, the ledger it last read, each open mission's Conductor presence and each mission's device answer, and makes views again only when one moved or a worker still being made stops counting against its cap; a closed mission's view is made again only when the book, its pull requests or its device's answer moved, and the worker registrations are read in one pass over the ledger for the nodes that name one.
The map is drawn from that section in two places: as a card in the front Agent tab's 보기 slot (`DetailItem::Mission`, opened by `detail_open` and kept, saved and dropped like every slot item, and taken out of every tab's slot when its mission is deleted), and on the page's mission screen (`web/src/MissionScreen.tsx`, PRD mission-screen), a screen of the page's own like the Overview and Desk, for which the core holds no state beyond which mission's events to send (below).
A lane saved on the retired Mission tool loads with no tool column (`workspace_views::Tool`).
Settings › Mission is `ui_state.conductor_settings`, saved in `core-state.json` as a plain value, as the 보기 slot is, so a stored value this build cannot read or refuses loads the defaults (`ui_state.conductor_settings_unknown`) and the rest of the saved UI state still loads; each edit sends only the fields it changes (`conductor_settings_set`). The cleanup switch `clean_merged` is read live by every mission, and a stored value from before it reads as on.
The map's direction `map_flow` (`down` or `across`, set from the map's own ↓ and → rather than the settings page) is one value for every mission's map; it is written only once it is `across`, so a build from before it still reads a file where no map was turned.
Fields a value kept by an earlier build may carry are left behind on load by `ConductorSettings::from_stored`, the one place any is still read, and the next save writes none: `checkers`, the review and verify defaults from before verification strength, so such a value reads as `normal`; `warn_review_fails` and `warn_quiet_minutes`, thresholds no edit could change and which are now fixed; and `other_vendor`, the switch for a checker of another kind of agent, which the Conductor now always prefers by `hide mission help`.
The cap is enforced where a spawn is reserved: `prepare_delivery` computes the spawn's `MissionAdmission` from the caller's open mission, and the ledger's reserve counts that mission's live workers under the same lock, so two spawns at once cannot both pass.
A take hands the mission's workers to the new Conductor in the ledger (`Mutation::AdoptMissionWorkers`), queued on the delivery worker before the take answers, so it lands before any command the new Conductor sends next; a mission spawn's reserve makes the same handover first, for a Conductor that registered only to start it.
Pull request wakes are decided on the GitHub ingest, compared with each of a node's pull requests' last seen head, review and merge, recorded on the mission (at most 32 unsent) until their letter is in the Conductor's inbox, and sent by `hide:conductor` from one thread of their own, at most 256 at a time.
The same thread sends the wakes Hide records for a node's sleeping worker (`request` letters, at most 16 waiting per mission) and the raises and closes it tells the Conductor of; a worker's letter the ledger refuses leaves the record and is raised to the Conductor.
A command whose change would take one mission past its 7 MiB write budget is undone and answered `mission_full`; deleting other missions does not make room in that file.
Deleting a Conductor's archived session deletes its missions in the same transition.
The book is schema 2 since node finish lines (PRD mission-map-git-criteria): `hide-core/src/mission_criteria.rs` holds the lines and their rules with no I/O, `runtime/mission_criteria.rs` the gates on a node's done and a close, the owner checks and the CI read, and `runtime/mission_outside.rs` the outside nodes ([hide-private missions.md: Finish lines](delivery.md#missions)).
A schema 1 book is converted as it is read: each mission becomes `exempt`, so nothing made before the gate is held by it, and a node's old one-string `criteria` becomes its one line; the read copies the file it read to `missions.v1.json` beside it (`hide_kit::layout::missions_before_criteria`) before anything saves schema 2, never replaces a copy already there, and logs `missions.converted` with whether the copy was written, so a build from before can be put back on it; a copy that cannot be written leaves the book unreadable and unchanged so the next start can retry the conversion.
A schema newer than this build stays unread, as any unreadable book does.
The book is schema 3 since PRD mission-node-simple: a node is `planned`, `working`, `done` or `dropped`, holds a list of pull requests with GitHub's last answer for each, and may carry one attention, the causes already raised, Hide's last act, the wakes it sent its worker and what became of its worktree.
A node's `launched` (`missions::NodeLaunch`) is an optional field of schema 3, which a build from before ignores and drops on its next save: `Runtime::record_node_launches` fills it from the pane launch records (`ui_state.pane_launches`) on the agent pass that settles them (`apply_pane_launches`), right after the settle, for any node whose worker has none, a closed mission's included so a mission that closed before its worker's proof still gets it, when the pane record's conversation is the worker registration's own; it looks again only when the launch records (every write counted in `launches_edit`, a wake's or a resume's as much as a settle's), the ledger or the book moved since it last looked (`launch_proof_made`), compares in memory under the lock and saves through the book's save thread, so it adds no read, process or timer.
A schema 2 book is moved as it is read (`convert_before_simple`, after `convert_before_criteria` for a schema 1 book) and the read copies the file to `missions.v2.json` beside it (`hide_kit::layout::missions_before_simple`) before anything saves schema 3, never replacing a copy already there, as `missions.v1.json` is kept; the event files read their old node statuses the same way without being rewritten.
The book is schema 4 since PRD mission-human-gate: a node's line may be its gate (`human`, below), with where its pass came from (`via`) and the decision that asks it (`asked`); a schema 3 book reads unchanged, with no gate, and the read copies the file to `missions.v3.json` beside it (`hide_kit::layout::missions_before_gates`) before anything saves schema 4, never replacing a copy already there.
A build from before gates finds schema 4 newer than itself and leaves the book unread, every mission command answering `mission_unavailable`, so going back to it means putting `missions.v3.json` back as `missions.json`, which loses what the missions did since.
What a mission does by itself and what it raises is one pure function, `hide-core/src/mission_health.rs`: it reads a mission and the facts beside it (GitHub's list when fresh, each node's worker life, the pull requests the worker's row lists as its own, the lines still open, whether the device answers) and answers acts, with no I/O.
`runtime/mission_health.rs` is its driver: it gathers those facts and applies the acts under `Mutex<Runtime>`, which costs a few comparisons and no process, read or write beyond the book's own save thread, and it runs from the coordinator's tick only when a fact it compared with the last evaluation moved, so it adds no watch loop.
What is slow stays off the lock: the project's pull request read the evaluation waits on is the ordinary GitHub read, asked again at most once in its own thirty seconds.
A done node's merged worktree is retired by `runtime/mission_cleanup.rs` while Settings › Mission's cleanup switch (`clean_merged`) is on: the evaluation chooses the worktrees under the lock from the book and GitHub's fresh answer, and one worker thread at a time retires at most 16 off the lock through `runtime/worktree_retire.rs`, the retire Hide AI's attempts share, which removes a worktree only when it is clean and holds no agent pane or running program and keeps the branch ([hide-private missions.md: What Hide settles in a mission by itself](delivery.md#missions)); off, the mission deletes no file.
A raise is its Conductor's to settle unless its reason is one the operator settles first (`AttentionReason::operator_first`: a gate with no Conductor, a Conductor's failure); the raises a Conductor has not settled are one derived safety net per mission (`mission_health::safety_net`, from the book, whether a Conductor is present, since when it has been, and the clock), drawn at once with no Conductor and once the oldest stood 20 minutes with one, never a stored state; the time a Conductor came back is kept in memory only, so a daemon restart counts it from the restart.
A raise to the operator is laid on a row by the same path as a plan review and a mission decision; when no row shown carries it, whether its owner is gone, working or registered with no row, the mission's view says so (`on_row`, read from the rows laid, and the notice claim lays them first) and the shell draws the mission itself in Needs You, and it is told once by a notice; the operator's choice is one typed event, `mission_attention`, applied under the lock.
A `check` line is judged against the commit the node's worker's checkout is at, read from the catalog Hide already holds for its pane, and a `ci` line against the pull request's head in the GitHub answer, so the gate starts no git or `gh` process under the lock.
The outside nodes are read off the lock on an issue worker, one read per project out at a time, after the GitHub ingest, the background fetch's answer and a change in the local worktree catalog; an outside pull request is a `gh pr view <n> --json state` allowlisted by `hide-node-link/src/gh.rs`, and an outside branch a few fixed git commands (`RefCommit`, `CountCommits`) on the project's node, against the default branch resolved to one commit, locally and as last fetched, once per read and after every branch head it compares.
A mission's events (PRD mission-plan-visibility D-15, D-22) are kept apart from the book, so its 7 MiB budget never counts them: `hide-core/src/mission_events.rs` holds the model and `MissionEventStore`, one save thread that writes each mission's file under `missions/events/` (`hide_kit::layout::mission_histories`) off the lock, collapsing a burst to one write per mission, deletes a gone mission's file, and is joined when the store drops; `runtime/mission_events.rs` decides which command makes which event under the lock.
The first migration reads the legacy `mission-events/` once and writes its histories into the folder before installing the index.
A failed history copy holds the index back; retry starts from the unchanged legacy histories.
Once the index exists, the old event directory is neither read nor swept, so a downgraded build can sweep or reuse an id without changing the folder book's history.
The lock hands the store only a change's new events: the thread keeps its own copy of each log, starting from the logs read at launch, and extends, encodes and writes it off the lock, so an event never copies or encodes a mission's history under `Mutex<Runtime>`.
The core holds each history as a shared list of shared events (`History`), so publishing the open mission's copies a pointer, and a change made while a published list is still held copies pointers, never the events.
A mission keeps at most 500, the oldest dropped and counted; the files are read back with the book at launch, a file that cannot be read is logged and replaced on its mission's next event, and the folder moves with the core (`MOVES_WITH_CORE`).
The events are published as their own rest section, `mission_events`, for one mission only: the one the mission screen's detail shows, which the page names with one typed event, `mission_shown` (`missions.shown`, held unsaved, only for a mission the book holds, and cleared when that mission is deleted; the page sends it again on every reconnect, and between windows the last word wins, PRD mission-screen D-16), else the one whose card is on top of the front Agent tab's drawn 보기 slot, which the core reads from its own slot (`refresh_mission_events`), made again only when that mission or its events changed, so a mission's history never rides every frame; the section shares the core's list and is encoded with the rest of the frame off the lock.
A node holds two more optional fields of schema 3, which a build from before ignores and drops on its next save: `steps`, the few lines its Conductor wrote with the plan (`NodeInput.steps`, at most 8 of at most 80 characters, refused as `mission_steps_invalid` with the node's key and a next action, never cut; a replan that leaves them out keeps them, an empty list clears them), and `brief`, the first prompt its worker was spawned on.
The node keeps `brief` because the delivery ledger lets a finished letter go a day after it ended (`delivery::RETENTION_MS`) and a mission lasts days: `mission node --agent-id` copies it from the spawn record whose child is the bound worker (`runtime/mission_brief.rs`, `worker_brief`), and a worker whose spawn kept none leaves the last one; a mission started before this build has none for its running nodes.
The map's `NodeView` carries `steps` and only the brief's size (`brief_bytes`), so a mission of sixty-four nodes never sends sixty-four briefs of up to 16 KiB; the text rides its own rest section, `mission_brief`, for the one node whose folded box the operator opened (`mission_brief_read`, one typed event that copies that node's text into the section, which the next read replaces), and the screen draws nothing for a node with no brief.
How a node's work goes is one source on the screen: the worker's own plan (`NodeView.plan`) once it exists, else `steps`; a worker step whose title is not one of `steps` is marked changed, and nothing writes the Conductor's steps into the worker's plan (`web/src/missions.ts`, `nodeSteps`).
The operator's answer to a decision is kept on the mission (`Answer`, keyed by the question it answers) and typed into the Conductor's conversation by the doorbell's thread (`delivery::doorbell`), which judges the Conductor's pane as it judges a letter's recipient, releases a draft by the same composer read and reads the composer again right before typing (`clear_to_type`, shared with the bell), and types off the lock; what it waits for (`AnswerHold`) and whether the operator pressed `지금 보내기` for it are memory only, so a restart shows it as sending until the next pass.
Once the prompt operation (`prompt_agent`) is asked, a failed, timed-out or unreadable reply may follow a typed answer, so the book holds the answer as `unconfirmed` before the prompt is asked (shown as sending until the engine replies, memory only) and no pass, and no restart after a stop in between, types it again; only the operator's `resend` from the banner makes it due once more (engineering principle 11).
What a decision shows the operator to look at is linked from facts the core already records, never guessed from a name or a time (`runtime/mission_views.rs`, operator decision 2026-11-09).
`stamp_control_opener`, the one path an agent's `hide file|diff|browser open` takes, hands the View to `link_mission_view`: a View the mission's Conductor opened is kept on the mission (`conductor_views`), and one opened by a working node's worker or an agent under it, found by walking the ledger's parents at most 32 deep, is kept on the node with its attempt (`views`), each list capped at 16 with the oldest dropped (`missions::VIEW_LINK_LIMIT`) and saved with the book, so a restart loses none and no agent runtime reports its turns.
The list is made when `decide` runs and kept on the question (`Question.views`): the Views `decide --show` names in the Conductor's checkout, in their order (the CLI opens a path as a View first and sends its id; an id no View there has is refused `mission_show_unknown`), then the Conductor's kept Views and the stopped node's Views of its current attempt that are still open, newest first, at most 16 in all; it empties the mission's list, so the next question starts from what the Conductor opens after this one, and the same question asked again with `--show` puts the named ones first.
The mission's list is the mission's and not one agent's, so a Conductor that takes the mission over asks with what its predecessor opened; nothing opened after `decide` joins the question.
Each of the question's links keeps what its View was when it was linked (`ViewLink.kept`: kind, name as its tab said it, address, and a diff's Changes group), read with `serde(default)` so a book written before reads with nothing kept and no schema raise; a name is cut at 256 characters, an address past 4096 is not kept, and an outside file, which only a window's grant names, keeps nothing (PRD mission-human-gate D-20).
`decision_views` lists every link of the question on the mission's view (`MissionView.decision_views`, with who linked it, `mission_decision_view_by`, and the opener's pane for the phone) until the question is answered or cleared: an open one from its View, the one the link names or, after it closed and opened again, the last-focused one showing the same document or page; a closed one from what the link kept, `closed`, under the link's own id; a closed link from a book that kept nothing is not listed.
`refresh_missions` compares the View layouts' change count as one more input only while an open decision links any, so a mission with none pays nothing for a View's change; the Conductor row's decision ask carries the count of the open ones (`views`), so a View closing changes the eye and nothing else.
Each link keeps the agent the View was open for when the decision linked it (`KeptView.opener`, by machine, engine terminal and session, never a pane id), and every row names its link by `view`, a token that tells two checkouts' Views apart without saying either path.
Pressing a row is one event, `mission_view_reopen` (the mission, the question's key, the row's `view` and, from the phone, a request id): an open View takes its area, and a closed one opens again from what the link kept, as the View of that agent if it had one, so it is in that agent's Files strip and phone 볼 것 again and is not raised as new.
Both are shown in the link's checkout brought forward with its device by one path (`reveal_in_checkout`): at once where the core brings the checkout forward or it is in front already, else after the device's engine is asked to bring it forward and the sync sees it land, as a reveal into a device's checkout does; a file goes through `reveal_path`, a page through `place_browser` with its reveal, a diff through `show_diff_in_view`.
A question that changed, a link that kept nothing, a checkout no longer listed, a reveal refused as it was asked or a file that could not be read opens nothing and goes to the diagnostic log (`mission.view_reopen_refused`).
A press with a request id keeps its outcome on the row (`DecisionView.reopens`, every kept press of that row, so two phones pressing it at once each find their own): refused, or still waiting until the row is open again; one still waiting after a device's answer and landing stages (20 s) ends refused, so no press waits for a View that never comes.
At most 16 presses are kept in memory (four for each of the four phones a Mac pairs); at the cap the oldest press that ended goes, a press still waiting is never pushed out, and with all 16 waiting a new press opens nothing and is logged (`mission_view_reopens_full`).
Linking marks no View seen or unseen and raises nothing: the row's read record, its descendant signals and the notices key on the row's state and the question, never on the count, so a View opened or closed while the question stands is no news.
With none linked the operator may ask for material once per question (`mission_material`, from the card or the phone's `ask_mission_material`): the core marks the question `material_asked` and records one `material_asked` wake keyed by the question, so a second press, from any surface, sends nothing, and the letter asks the Conductor for one page that opens with what changed, the 2-3 things to check and what good looks like, then to ask again with `--show`; the answer is never held back by it.
A node's gate (PRD mission-human-gate) is one more finish line, `human`, so the refusal of a node's done while a line is unmet holds it and every node behind it, and a mission or node without one is read, raised and settled as before.
The plan names it as the node's `gate`, one line of at most 80 characters (`mission_criteria::GATE_CHARS`), checked by `missions::check_gate` and kept by `mission_criteria::set_gate`; a replan that leaves it out keeps it and `null` takes it away, on a node not yet done.
`runtime/mission_gates.rs` owns it at run time, under the lock and from what the core holds: after each health evaluation `raise_gates` asks a gate whose node's other lines are all met through the mission's own decision (`Question` with the node, the two fixed choices and the Views a `decide` would link), once the decision is free, and withdraws a question whose gate is no longer reached; with no Conductor present, a gate that waits is also the mission's raise to the operator (`AttentionReason::HumanGate`, with no choice of its own, since the decision card answers it), which a Conductor coming back takes off.
