The node compares a key's pane with the keyboard's pane as the core last told it (`TerminalControl::Focus`, sent when the snapshot a screen reads shows the keyboard moved, by a key or not: the engine's own focus move, a close focusing a neighbour, the editor taking it), so the operator's next key into a pane the keyboard left moves it back however long they kept typing there (B1).
Labels' submit time, the doorbell's draft hold and its 30-second quiet wait read the same facts they did before, a second late at most, and no key takes the core's lock or publishes a snapshot (B5).
Reports reach the core through `hide_core::terminal_reports`: sending never waits for the runtime lock, and one thread takes them into the runtime in batches and notifies once per batch.
Past 16,384 waiting reports a report takes the place of the waiting one about the same subject (a pane's state, first frame, shown frame or keys, a paste's result, a creation's discard), so the core still ends at each node's last word; only a report about a subject none waiting names adds to the queue, and past 65,536 such a report is dropped with a `terminal.report_dropped` diagnostic.

| Goes to the core (control) | Goes between the screen and a node without the core (data) |
| --- | --- |
| Which panes attach and are released (`ATTACHED_TAB_LIMIT`, `released`), shown, asleep or closing; Reconnect | Keys (`key`), from the web socket to the router to the pane's writer |
| PTY size (`terminal_resize`), from the screen that last sent the pane input (`pane_sizes.rs`), the moment that screen's view fits its drawn rectangle | Pane output, from the session's reader to the hub to the client (`terminal` frames) |
| Wheel (`terminal_scroll`) and a pointer event (`terminal_mouse`) | A view's grid and whether it has nothing drawn (`terminal_viewport`), which the node's attach rules read |
| Creation requests keys are sent against: opened, resolved to a pane, discarded | Held keys and a paste's text with the keys behind it, written by the node's writer |
| Input facts: when the operator typed and whether it submitted; attach state, first frame, notes and errors | Redraw requests from the hub to the pane's node |
| A paste's admission, preparation, transfer and cancellation (`runtime/attachments.rs`) | A device's terminal lines inside its node link |
| Every node call (`Call::*`): files, folders and documents (`RootOpen`, `List`, `Stamps`, `Bytes`, `Index`, `OpenDocument`, `Revision`, `Save`, `Create`, `Rename`, `Move`, `Trash`, `Directory`, `RealPaths`, `PathFacts`, `JudgeFolders`, `SetAsideFolder`, `DrainTrash`), Git and projects (`Changes`, `Project`, `Worktrees`, `BranchCheck`, `Registrable`, `WorktreeRemove`, `WorktreeRemovalCheck`, `WorktreesRegistered`, `IgnoredRepository`, `ProjectCreate`, `Repository`, `WorktreeRemoveClean`, `WorktreeRetire`, `BranchFacts`, `BranchDiff`, `BranchMerge`, `BranchDiscard`, `BranchCatchUp`, `RepositoryClone`, `Git`, `GitWatch`, `Gh`, `HomeSync`), the kit (`Kit`, `HookDiagnosis`, `AgentInstalled`), the AI CLIs (`AiAvailability`, `AiModels`, `AiExecute`, `AiMeasurement`, `AiRestart`, `AiRelease`, `UsageLimitFetch`), processes (`TerminateGroup`, `ProcessStarts`, `ProcessDescendants`, `ListeningPorts`), disk (`DiskUsage`, `VolumeFree`), sessions and the link record (`LabelTranscript`, `SessionActivity`, `SessionThread`, `LinkFiles`, `LinkRead`, `SessionWorkTurn`, `ProjectSessions`, `SessionStat`, `SessionText`, `SessionConversation`), attachments (`ReadAttachments`, `StageAttachment`, `RemoveAttachments`, `RemoveClipboard`), the services a link starts (`Hello`, `PanesStart`, `TerminalsStart`) and `Cancel` | A device pane's `hide` command streams (`StreamWrite`, `StreamClose` down, `StreamOpen`, `StreamData`, `StreamClosed` up), which hided serves as `/ws` connections, and its pane proofs (`PaneProof` up, `PaneProofAnswer` and `PaneInspect` down), which hided's credential registry answers |
| A device's engine session and the SSH file transfer of a paste (`hide_node_link::device`), through the core's device connector | |

Two terminal facts stay core-routed on purpose: the PTY size, because which screen's view sizes the pane is the core's decision (the one that last sent it input), not any view's, and the wheel, because whether it scrolls the pane's view or reaches the pane's own mouse mode is a decision about the pane, not a byte for it.

### Agent labels in the core


The current pane binding and conversation display record are separate (`labels/record.rs`).
The links ledger stores bounded title, goal, summary, analyzed-turn hashes and PR sightings under its existing device/provider/native-ID key; its single writer, schema migration, deletion and retention remain the owners.
`LedgerCall::Metadata` is a local, bounded query through the existing mailbox, with a one-second response deadline, performed only by the labels reader off the coordinator and Runtime lock.
An already read owner reuses its in-memory metadata, and an unchanged display is not enqueued again.
Legacy compatibility candidates are capped at 512 short records and twenty PRs per record, contain no paths or raw facts, and are imported only after an exact native owner match.
A metadata write requires an indexed session so it cannot create an orphan outside existing retention.

When the engine reports no session reference, that same reader may ask it for the session the pane's foreground program names (`Engine::resumed_session`), with a one-second deadline.
It accepts only the adapter's executable and explicit resume selector within 64 arguments and 8 KiB, refusing forks, conflicting candidates and unbounded input.
The native owner proves the historical record, not the current process conversation; an argv-only locator remains unconfirmed and never feeds analysis, current turn facts or control.
A hook reference takes priority immediately and advances the generation before reading; a successful current native read confirms that binding.
The core carries the display connection state into shared rows, and UI controls continue to use the existing current-pane authority.
Failures retain dimmed display history and retry on the existing worker at fifteen seconds, without another thread or retry queue.
Unreadable and unknown-version labels files disable that instance's file writes while runtime observation continues, preserving their original bytes.
The turn card's facts ride the same pane record and the same reads, with no new read, call or AI request: the session facts keep the head of the agent's last message after the operator's last request and after the newest one (`SessionFacts::replies`, two at most, each its first two lines, its length and its time), the record keeps the newest four turns the label judged to end on a question whoever began them (`PaneRecord::asked`, a device's in its mark), since a lead's letter turns are not kept in `recent_turns`, and each kept turn keeps the witness of its text at its judged end (`RecentTurn::witness`); a new session or a rewritten conversation drops them with the turns.


What each Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode pane is doing (the session's goal, one line for its turn, and how the turn ended) is made by the core, not by a plugin and not through pane tokens (PRD labels-in-hided, overview-request-view D-08).
The code is `hide-core/src/labels/`.
Each session-sync coordinator, one per engine (this Mac's and each connected device's), owns a `LabelWorker` it feeds from the agent state it already follows; the core owns one `LabelAnalyzer` for all of them and one `LabelStore`.
No read or analysis runs under the runtime mutex: conversation reads run on the worker's reader thread, analyses on the analyzer's thread, and the coordinator hands the runtime their result with the session payload (`LabelWorker::overlay`), which the pass lays on the payload in the same step under the lock that observes it for delivery (`LabelOverlay::apply`, memory work only), so the projection is where a label becomes the row's title, sentences and question.

- **When it reads.** A pane's conversation is read only when its agent status, engine state sequence or session reference moved, when an earlier read left a backlog, when a provider wait ran out, and once about three seconds after a turn starts whose prompt was not written yet.
  A read is bounded and resumable, from the checkpoint the store kept, so an unchanged pane spends no read, no engine call, no request and no publish.
- **What it reads.** `hide_session::label_transcript::read` is the session adapter (PRD overview-request-view D-14): it proves the provider's native owner of the session the engine's reference names, and returns the same facts for every agent, whatever its format: the session's own title (Claude Code's `ai-title` and the operator's `custom-title`, Codex's newest `thread_name` in `session_index.jsonl`, OpenCode's session `title`), each person's message with its time, its image count and the coordination sender its header names, each assistant message, the pull request addresses its tools printed with the time they were printed (Claude Code's subagent files under `<session>/subagents/` included, the 16 most recently written files and 2 MiB a read, the rest reported as `subagent_files_capped`), and the next checkpoint.
  OpenCode's database is read in the same bounds, each row's size answered from its record header before anything is loaded: a message row over 64 KiB (`message_capacity`), a part row over 256 KiB (`part_capacity`) and a row holding no text (`not_text`) are skipped unread, one read admits at most 1 MiB including metadata, IDs and 64 bytes per part before retaining or parsing payloads, and leaves the rest for the next (a part the first message of a read cannot fit is `read_budget`), and the title is cut to 512 characters in the query (one too long to cut there is no title).
  The part-size preflight visits only the next bounded set: at most 256 parts per message and 512 parts per read, including empty, malformed and skipped parts, plus one header-only cap probe per message.
  Crossing the message cap reports `part_work_capacity` and advances past that message; reaching the read cap defers the next message to the next read.
  A read-only transaction also limits SQLite scans and sorts to approximately one million virtual-machine instructions through its progress handler; missing indexes or excessive database work return `opencode_db_work_capacity` without changing the provider database.
  The ordered queries stream row headers, and metadata, message IDs and parts consume the same cumulative byte budget before their payload query or JSON parsing, including malformed metadata and the first record.
  OpenCode 2.x's `session_message` rows are read in the same bounds, with a content item standing where a part does and an 8 MiB scan limit for a row that holds its whole content (the reader paragraph under Agent adapters above).
  Text an agent wraps around an attachment (Codex's `<image ...>` blocks and file list) and text it injects (hook context, `<system-reminder>`, a compaction request) are no one's message.
  Text the agent itself writes on the person's side is no one's message: Claude Code's hook, meta and system prompts and its compaction summary (`isCompactSummary`, `isVisibleInTranscriptOnly`, which otherwise look like a typed prompt), and Codex's `compacted` record with the earlier requests it replays.
  A Claude Code command is the operator's request only when it went to the model: one Claude Code answers itself with a `<local-command-stdout>` record (`/model`) is not, unless that answer carries `turnOrigin: "human"`, the mark Claude Code writes when it then hands the turn to the model (`/goal`, 2.1.294-2.1.301); `CommandReply::after` in `hide-session/src/lib.rs` reads the mark.
  A Codex user message wrapped in `<codex_internal_context source="...">` is Codex's own text unless its source is `user_goal`, whose `User set the goal: "<JSON string>"` objective is the operator's request (the message stays as written when there is no quoted objective, as for one Codex omitted); `codex_internal_context` is the one place that reads this format (codex-cli 0.163.0, `hide-session/tests/fixtures/adapters/codex-0.163.0-goal/`).
  Only tool output is scanned for addresses (`hide-session/src/sightings.rs`), on the records the read already decodes, at most eight per output; an address in a reply or a request is a mention.
  OpenCode keeps its sessions in `opencode.db` under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode`, or `~/.local/share/opencode` when that is unset, which the adapter opens read-only with a 50 ms busy wait: a locked database is a skipped read (`opencode_db_busy`) retried on the next state change, never a wait OpenCode feels, and an assistant message without `time.completed` is left for the next read.
  The SQLite URI also sets `readonly_shm=1`, so a read never creates or updates OpenCode's WAL index; an unavailable index refuses the read while the live database retains its normal locking.
  `hide-session/tests/it/adapters.rs` is the contract every adapter passes, against a fixture in the agent's own format at the version it names (`hide-session/tests/fixtures/adapters/`); a format the adapter cannot read leaves that pane's row with the engine's facts only and a diagnostic.
  `hide-session/src/envelope.rs` attributes only the first nonempty line's current `Hide letter <id> from <name> (<agent>) [<kind>]` header, preserving the first sender when several letters arrive together.
  `contracts/delivery-envelope.json` independently pins examples for both this reader and `delivery::mailbox::pull`; older delivery headers have no special sender interpretation.
  It reads only under the agent's own transcript root in its HOME (`.claude/projects` or `.codex/sessions`), after every link in the path is resolved, and takes an id only as letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`; anything else is refused with a stable code that names no path (`label_session_outside_roots`, `label_session_id_invalid`).
  For this Mac it runs in process.
  For a device the same function runs in `hided node serve` behind the `label_transcript` call (since protocol 12, with the adapter's facts since 14); the events come to this Mac in memory only and are never stored (only the marks under What is kept are), and the analysis runs on this Mac's provider login.
  A device whose helper is not connected keeps its panes' labels and is retried every fifteen seconds; a helper too old to know the call leaves the provider name, and the device's kit status already offers the reinstall that replaces it.
- **What the last turn waits for.** The same read folds Claude and Codex native turn records into an agent-neutral turn tracker (`hide-session/src/turns.rs`), answering whether an unanswered native question or completed plan waits for the operator.
  Native tool-call ids correlate question results; ordinary prose never supplies structured question content.
  Codex's `request_user_input_async` is the one question whose tool result is not the answer: the tracker keeps its waiting question numbers (at most eight per call) and each `<send_user_message_question_reply>` message names one by `questionItemId`; the message is one of `INJECTED_PREFIXES`, so it is not a person's turn.
  The tracker bounds native call identities to 256 bytes, and a longer id fails the read explicitly.
  It keeps at most eight question calls per turn, and an answered call leaves to make room for a new one, so an interview that asks and answers one question after another never fills it.
  A ninth call while eight still wait makes what the turn waits for not known until the next turn starts or a person writes, and the read goes on: a failed read is read again from the same place, so it would never reach the message that ends it, and the session's labels and doorbell would stop for good.
  Optional `UserTurnContent` keeps at most 8 KiB of text and eight 256-byte choices, preserving UTF-8 boundaries and marking cuts.
  A native record beyond the separate 256 KiB physical-line admission cap is discarded without its body, and the bounded ids its structure carries become the record's turn mark: a tool result answers its call, an `AskUserQuestion` or `request_user_input` call waits with its content absent, a `request_user_input_async` call is not known (its question count decides which replies end the wait), and a Codex plan, start, completion or abort keeps its turn id and mode.
  An id past the native bounds is the same reported failure it is in a retained record.
  A record whose text is past the cap, such as a person's message with a pasted screenshot, keeps the tool marks its structure certifies and loses its text to labels and search, counted as `conversation_capacity` in the read's skip diagnostic.
  For Claude Code the scan also keeps the `name` and `id` of each `tool_use` block, and the `tool_use_id` of each `tool_result`, so a record too large to keep still pairs its calls with their results; the wake reader folds a lost wake mark for a record that may have carried a task's words and one the scan cannot follow, and nothing for one that can carry none (a screenshot), told by the record's kind and the call it answers and never by searching its words (`turns/wake.rs::Record`, [status-model.md](status-model.md#a-quiet-row-that-waits)).
  The marks only text gives, a person's message or an interruption, clear or end a wait and never start one, so losing them can hold a bell but never ring one into a menu.
  A record the scan cannot structure (an envelope it does not know, an escaped discriminator, an escaped or non-ASCII id, nesting past 64 levels) is skipped the same way and folds an unreadable mark: what the turn waits for is not known until the next turn starts or a person writes.
  Neither stops the read, because Claude Code writes a screenshot inline as base64, in a tool result or a person's message, and refusing one record would stop every later read of the session, its labels and its doorbell.
  A checkpoint an older scan took inside such a record kept no ids, so the cursor rereads that record from its start.
  Grok's records are read by its own scan instead (`grok::LargeLine`, above), which keeps a prompt's, answer's or question's turn effect without its text, because Grok also writes a pasted image inline.
  The tracker rides on the read's request and answer beside the checkpoint, so an incremental read continues the turn it was in, a read from the start or a rescan starts over, and a record replayed from the anchor is not folded twice.
  The record keeps the tracker and the engine's `state_change_seq` the read was asked under (`PaneRecord::turns`, `turns_seq`, set only once the backlog is read), and the overlay answers the wait (`LabelOverlay::waiting`) only for that state and the proven session, so a fact read for an earlier state never stands for a newer one.
  The turn end of an agent whose read reports background tasks is owed that read from the moment the engine reports the stop (`PaneRecord::turn_end_owed`, not saved); the overlay lays it as `RowFacts.turn_end_unread` for that state and `agent_activity` keeps the row Working until the read lands, fails or the agent runs again, so a stop that a proven task takes back is never announced ([status-model.md](status-model.md#a-quiet-row-that-waits)).
  A failed reread invalidates that proof and publishes no structured fact, while retaining the bounded tracker/checkpoint for a later successful continuation and the existing unavailable-read retry interval.
  A restart resumes without a read only when the wait was read for the stored state; a record from before turns were read is read once, from its anchor, where the turn's mode is not seen and the wait stays not known until the engine's next state.
  A device helper answers the same field; one that predates it answers without it, which reads as not known.
  The coordinator takes the overlay before delivery observes the payload, and the doorbell holds on a wait or on not knowing (`docs/delivery.md`, A menu the engine reads as a stop); the sidebar draws the typed question or approval and carries `user_turn` only for the proven current session/state (`docs/status-model.md`).
- **Who sent a request.** The engine's input calls name no sender, so the core keeps when the operator submitted to a pane through Hide (PRD overview-request-view D-19): a keyboard chunk of at most 64 bytes holding a carriage return outside a bracketed paste and not after `ESC`, which the pane's node reports as a submitted input fact (`TerminalReport::Input`, for this Mac's and a device's panes alike; see The terminal path), and a phone reply the engine accepted (`pane_input_submitted`, which hided dispatches after the engine takes the reply).
  An Enter at a prompt the engine reports `blocked` is not one; an Enter at a plan waiting for approval is, since Codex writes the next turn's message from it.
  Only the moment and whether the agent was running are kept, in memory, at most 32 per pane and 512 panes (`labels/input.rs`), behind a lock of its own that the runtime takes inside its mutex and the workers take alone.
  Each person's message is judged once and the verdict kept by its offset (`labels/facts.rs`): the coordination sender; else the operator when an unclaimed submit came at most two minutes before it (thirty while the agent was running, since a queued prompt is written when the agent takes it up); else, for a message older than this worker's view of the pane, the operator unless it is a delegated child's first request; else another agent.
  The first request is the first one any read holds, recorded once and kept across restarts (`first_request_offset`, set by the first read that holds a request, not by the read from the start), because Grok and OpenCode write the session before the prompt.
  A submit two messages could claim goes to the earlier and writes `requester.ambiguous`.
- **One analysis at a time.** `LabelAnalyzer` takes jobs in arrival order through one `hide-ai` router built from the operator's current provider and model choice, which it re-reads from the runtime before each analysis, so a change in Settings applies from the next analysis and the one running finishes on the choice it started with.
  Each worker hands in at most one job, so arrival order is a round robin between servers.
  Shutdown cancels the running request, which ends its provider child, and joins the thread.
  The prompts and schemas are `context_label.v26` (`context_label.rs`), one pair per boundary, and each asks only what its boundary can know; they name no language, and each request carries the core's output language, which the worker takes with the agent-summary switch on every tick ([AI_PROVIDERS.md](AI_PROVIDERS.md#the-output-language)).
  The turn's start answers `goal` (8 to 30 characters in Korean, Simplified Chinese and Japanese and 8 to 60 in English, what the session is to have made, or null until work is assigned), `goal_update` (`keep`, `refine` or `replace`) and `line` (at most 40 characters, 80 in English, the turn's work), and its end is `working` by construction, never the model's word, because how the turn will end is not known yet.
  A null goal leaves the existing title priority in place; it cannot clear an accepted goal, and an answered greeting with no required next action has an empty line and a stopped end of `done`.
  The turn's end answers the same three, its line the turn's result, what the operator is to answer or what the turn waits for, and `end`: `question`, `blocked`, `waiting`, `unfinished` or `done`, which split a stopped turn by whose move is next (the operator's; the operator's again, on a cause the line can state in one sentence that stopped the turn; something else's, such as a background test, build, CI run or another agent the turn started or handed work to, never a pull request, even when the turn only reported progress; nobody's on unfinished work; nobody's on finished work) and are taken in that order when more than one fits; a question with no line is read as done, a block with no line as unfinished, and a turn is `done` only when it reported its work finished.
  An answer outside its boundary's schema, a turn end that says `working` or a turn start that judges a turn's end, is refused by the router's schema check and by the parser and takes the failure path below; it is never read as another word.
  A record a `context_label.v5` turn end left as `working` keeps it until that pane's next analysis, and needs no conversion: a stopped agent's `working` end moves no verb and no group.
  A `v6` record keeps its end until that pane's next analysis and needs no conversion; the `v6` answers are all words `v8` still has.
  `blocked` names a cause the operator must act on and lands on the existing `error` demand wire value (the English word is Blocked); the background tasks a row waits on are not asked of the model but proven from the session's records (`hide-session/src/turns/wake.rs`, Claude Code only; [status-model.md](status-model.md) on a quiet row that waits), and the reply a row waits on comes from the delivery ledger when the runtime lays lineage (`runtime/agents.rs::lay_reply_waits`).
  The context carries the operator's requests only (D-09): the person's messages whose verdict is the operator's, the session's first request, and any not judged yet (`SessionFacts::feeds_analysis`), the first three and last eight of them or, once a goal exists, the previous goal, at most 800 masked characters of the requests and early replies that establish and clarify its assignment (`PaneRecord::goal_evidence`) and the new ones; then the latest exchange, because the line and the end judge the turn.
  The whole context is at most 4,000 characters (`MAX_ANALYSIS_CONTEXT_CHARS`), and each of its two sections is masked and cut on its own (`analysis.rs::bounded_context`): the requests section keeps its head within 2,000 characters, so the first request always stays, and the latest exchange keeps its tail in what is left, so a long exchange (Codex's 6,400-character goal reminder) never pushes the operator's requests out; a cut section ends or begins with `…`.
  The ledger's side of a turn-end request (`work_context`) is appended after that bound, as before.
  Before that context reaches the provider, secrets and emails are masked, the home-account prefix in macOS `/Users/example/`, Linux `/home/example/`, and Windows `C:\Users\example\` or `C:/Users/example/` paths becomes `~` for a bare home or `~/` before a tail, including homes at sentence ends and in `file://` requests, with surrounding prose, sentence punctuation, quote delimiters and the remaining tail unchanged, and other paths stay as written (`labels/analysis.rs`); the goal prompt excludes file paths.
  A turn uses the existing start/end schedule and costs no additional request to refine its goal.
  `keep` ignores the returned goal; `replace` changes the assignment only on its first analysis, at the start of an operator turn, or at the end of such a turn whose start was never asked (it ended within `START_DELAY`), and that end sees the new requests the start would have.
  `refine` can clarify a vague name at either boundary of an operator turn while the result still describes that turn; it preserves the whole assignment, and another agent's message cannot rename it.
  Specific names stay stable, and the line states a concrete action, finding, result or dependency rather than an acknowledgment.
  The assignment evidence is kept across local restarts, replaced with a new assignment, cleared on session reset, and excluded from device marks.
  Evidence refresh is limited to its original turn, so later pruning cannot replace saved clarification with a path-only request; an accepted new assignment replaces it even when the displayed title is unchanged.
  A named legacy record without this evidence has an unknown assignment origin and rolls from its current goal and latest exchange, without backfilling the session's first request as the current assignment.
  An accepted first or new assignment records evidence only when one new attributed request proves its origin; several historical requests do not.
  Both requests ask Codex for `medium` effort, as the first agent or the fallback, and ask Claude for none (`context_label::CODEX_EFFORT`; [AI_PROVIDERS.md](AI_PROVIDERS.md) owns the measurement).
  A line longer than its language's limit is cut between words and ends in `…` (`analysis.rs::truncate_phrase`, the goal's rule), never refused or emptied, so a long question stays a question.
  A turn is known by the person's message that began it, its time and its words (`turn_key`), so the key holds while the answer grows and moves once at the next message, even one that repeats the last word for word, such as a second letter notice or the same short reply; Cursor stamps that time to the minute, so there two identical messages within one minute stay one turn.
  A failure clears the turn's line and end and keeps the goal, so the row shows its facts and never stops on a guess (B20); a turn end that ran out of time is asked once more (D-33); one the environment can clear (no login, a usage limit, no provider, an over-budget refusal) asks again after the provider's reset time or ten minutes, and one the input settles parks that turn (`AnalysisFailure::retry_after`; [AI_PROVIDERS.md](AI_PROVIDERS.md#retry-policy) owns the router's side).
- **The switch.** Settings › Hide AI › Features › Agent summaries (`AiSettings::agent_summary` in `ai.json`, on by default, D-11) is read from the runtime by each coordinator on every tick and publish (`LabelWorker::set_summaries`).
  Off, the worker asks for nothing, the analyzer answers a queued job as stopped and cancels the running one (`LabelAnalyzer::cancel_running`), and the overlay lays no goal, line or end, so every surface shows the session's own title and the request view its facts; reads go on, because the rows stand on them.
  On again, the stored labels show at once and each pane's current turn is asked for, never the turns that ended while it was off.
- **Only for the session it was proven for.** A record stores the provider's native owner, proven from transcript metadata, and the reference it was proven under.
  A path reference yields a native session id only after the reader confirms it from that file's own metadata and the id hashes to the same provider owner.
  Claude Code's id is read from the first person's or assistant's record and Codex's from its `session_meta` record, scanning from the head of the file; a record over the 256 KiB line cap on the way, such as a first message carrying pasted images, is read to its newline and dropped, not refused, and the scan as a whole stops at the 64 MiB whole-file read cap, so a session that opens with a screenshot is still proven and its turn read (`hide-session/src/source/facts.rs`).
  A record that names the session at a fixed place cannot be passed over: Codex's `session_meta`, a Pi or omp header and Grok's `summary.json` hold no pasted content and are read up to the 1 MiB naming cap (`hide_session::NAMING_RECORD_LIMIT_BYTES`, the thread header's earlier cap, now every reader's), and one over it is refused with that size as its reason (`session_capacity:line_bytes:1048576`); a Pi or omp header, which the format requires as its first line, is left as soon as the read crosses the cap and never read to its end, while a search for Codex's `session_meta` or a thread's header passes a larger record before it and is refused for size only when nothing after names the session; a discovery charges every byte it read for a candidate, what it read past the header and a refused candidate's too, to its one budget, reads a candidate from a 1 KiB first block so a rejected one spends little more than its header, and stops once the budget is spent, so a folder of oversized headers costs the budget and one naming record, a refusal row in the session listing, never a session the lookup calls missing or one the listing leaves out without a word; Grok's `plan_mode.json` keeps its own small cap (`label_session_metadata_line_capacity`).
  The optional id is retained with that proof and projected only while the current reference still proves it; a switched path exposes no previous identity, and a retained helper answer without the field grants no path identity.
  The projection shows a label only while the pane's current engine reference proves that owner, so a new session, a reused pane, a provider change and an A to B to A switch show nothing of the previous session until the new one is proven, and returning to the same session restores its label (`PaneRecord::proven_for`).
  Every read and analysis result carries the pane's generation, which moves with the reference, and a late result for an earlier generation is dropped.
  Nothing is exchanged through pane tokens, so there is no token fence or publication guard to keep in step.
- **What is kept.** `labels.json` in the daemon's state folder, beside `core-state.json`, written whole through a temporary file and a rename with mode 0600, outside the runtime mutex, keeps per local pane the proven owner, label, analyzed turns, the read checkpoint, the time the core saw the pane change state and the session's facts (its titles, the last request the operator sent and the last someone else sent with their requesters, each cut to 8 KiB, the time of the agent's last reply without its words (idle-agent sleep counts from it), the newest 20 pull request addresses and the subagent checkpoints), limited to panes the server still lists.
  Device records stay in memory, including during later local saves, and the device helper is read again after a restart; loading an older store removes its device records and rewrites the private file.
  The one thing of a device that is written is its `devices` marks: per pane the session proof (a hash token), the hashes of the turns already analyzed, how the last turn ended, the label the model wrote (goal and line, which are its own words and capped) and the time the pane changed state, never a request, reply, path or fact of the conversation.
  A restart restores them so a device turn that was already analyzed is not asked of the model again (75 of 375 label requests in one log window had repeated) and its label is still shown.
  At most 512 panes of a device and 64 devices are kept, the newest first, and a save that changes no mark writes nothing (a pane's state change or a new fact of the conversation alone does not rewrite the file).
  One mark this build cannot read is dropped alone with a `store.device_marks_dropped` diagnostic, and a cap that drops marks writes `store.device_marks_capped`.
  A core move drops the section (`node_migration/reown.rs`).
  Native-proven display metadata waits for the shared links ledger in one pending value per device/provider/native session, at most 512 per label worker, independently of the source pane's lifetime or later conversation.
  The existing reader commits one value at a time and acknowledges it only after the indexed-only ledger writer returns; a newer pending value survives an older acknowledgement, and unavailable or unindexed saves retry on the existing 15-second tick.
  Each pane submits a candidate only when its observed display changes; an acknowledgement rechecks capacity without turning unchanged values from other panes of the same conversation into new writes.
  The pending set contains only bounded display fields and identity, never a path or conversation facts; it is not another persistent store and adds no worker or timer.
  A first save whose history read failed merges existing analysis and PR history before writing while preserving the current native title and manual-title clear.
  Capacity and write failures reach the existing diagnostic log, and native reads retain priority over waiting writes.
  Once imported, a restart resumes from it with no analysis request for an unchanged pane; a file that cannot be read starts empty and records a diagnostic, and nothing in it is shown until a reference proves it.
  The first run with no `labels.json` imports the retired plugin's `display-state.json` once, taking only entries it had proven an owner for.
- **One generator per engine.** A worker generates only while the node on the machine that runs its engine holds that engine's lock for it (`Call::LabelLock`, `hide_host::label_lock`): an exclusive `flock` on `<engine folder>.hide-label-generator.lock` beside the engine's folder, which every daemon opening that folder shares whatever HOME it runs with, so cores on any machine that label one engine meet at one file and the core keeps no lock file of its own.
  The node keys each lock by the engine folder as the core named it, and a node that dialed its core locks only its own engine's file.
  The core's own node answers at once; a device's or an inbound node's answer crosses its link, so that ask runs on a thread of its own and wakes the worker, because the worker runs on the session-sync thread.
  Until the first answer the worker shows the labels it stored, and an ask that failed (a device still connecting) is tried again after 2 s; only a node that names no server, or one on a protocol that predates the call, has no lock to share, and any other refusal fails the ask.
  A second core on the same server shows provider names, logs `generator.standby` and asks again every thirty seconds, so it takes over when the first one ends; the holder asks again on the same beat, because a node lets its locks go with the link it served.
  The node holds each lock for the worker that took it, so a worker's late give-back never frees its successor's lock, and it unlocks explicitly when the worker or the link ends, so a descriptor inherited by a concurrently starting child cannot extend the role; a node that serves no engine it can name has nothing shared to lock, and its worker generates.
- **Status.** The question state, an unfinished turn and a wait on something other than a pull request come from the analysis's `end`; blocked, working, done and idle come only from the engine's `agent_status`.
  A `labels.json` written before v5 keeps its `task` as the goal and its `progress` as the line, and a pending question becomes `end: question` with its reply as the line (`PaneRecord::upgrade_v3`); that transition goes when no v3 record is left to read.
  An agent that is working, or whose engine state sequence moved while it was stopped and is stopped or blocked again, ran in between and is no longer asking, so its question and requested reply end.
  Nothing reads `status_*` tokens, and nothing produces the Error demand any more.
- **Time.** The core projects `last_prompt_at_unix_ms` from the latest nonzero timestamp among the proven session's native operator and other-agent requests; a real request letter counts, while hook, system, compaction and tool records do not.
  Project and Task rows, including their children, draw elapsed time from that value on one shared one-second clock (`web/src/components/elapsed.tsx`); unknown time draws nothing, and a ticking display causes no session read, save or snapshot.
  State changes and daemon startup never replace the prompt time: `changed_at_unix_ms`, recency ordering and request-wait clocks retain their separate state semantics.
  Existing local request facts restore the same prompt time after restart; connected-device facts stay memory-only and restore after the helper rereads the session.
  Native ownership fences every projection, a new session drops the previous facts, and a rewritten transcript rebuilds both requester categories so a removed request cannot leave its timestamp behind.
- **Diagnostics.** Reads, discarded results, provider waits and standby go to `Logs/core.jsonl` with `component` `labels`, a pane and generation, and never conversation text, secrets or paths; a failure the operator cannot act on never reaches the screen.

`hide-core/src/labels/tests.rs` owns the behavior and `desktop/e2e/session-labels.spec.ts` proves it end to end; [status-model.md](status-model.md#task-identity) names the regression owners.

### Optional private features

The public workspace and the official free app do not link a Factory engine or expose Factory commands.
A separate private repository keeps the removed implementation and internal development resources.
There is no runtime replacement or Pro protocol in this release.
The legacy store files are preserved during core moves; their presence starts no engine.
Memory retires its own worktrees through the ordinary `Call::WorktreeRetire` machine operation.

### The mobile companion

On macOS, Windows and Linux, turn on Mobile in Settings and scan its QR with the phone camera to open `app.withhide.dev`.
No Tailscale installation, Hide account or payment is needed for the default relay connection.
The phone and the computer encrypt their messages before sending them through Hide's relay in Tokyo.
The relay passes those encrypted messages between them and cannot read conversations, commands or phone credentials; it sees routing identifiers, connection times and traffic sizes.
The computer must remain awake and connected; the relay stores no messages to deliver later.
Tailscale remains an advanced direct option, with its system support recorded in [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md#what-each-system-supports).

The shared relay library and its WASM boundary are specified in [RELAY_PROTOCOL.md](RELAY_PROTOCOL.md).
The hosted phone uses its WASM initiator.
hided uses it for signed device admission, Noise responder sessions and QR v2; the phone credential is checked only inside the established encrypted session.

Phone transport, pairing, conversation reads and delivery live in `hided/src/mobile/`; status projection and notification transitions belong to `hide-core/src/agent_state/`.
The phone's own language and light or dark choice are the one exception to "the core owns the preference": they belong to that phone's browser, in `web/src/mobile/settings.ts` (storage key `hide.phone.settings`), and are never sent to hided.
The loader and the app read the same module, so the start page and every protocol bundle of an origin agree; the app's language is that choice, else the core's `interface_language`, else the phone's language, and `followPhoneTheme` is the one function that puts the `dark` class on the page.
Mobile is off until the operator turns it on in Settings > Mobile, and it is kept in `mobile.json` beside the daemon's state (the switch, selected method, last direct scope, push mode, owned serve entry, VAPID key, device signing seed and Noise static key), written through a temporary file at mode 0600.
An older file without a method keeps Tailscale when it has a Serve record or last tailnet; a new setup defaults to relay.
The relay keys are decoded once per daemon and shared by admission, QR and push payloads.

The default transport is `mobile/relay.rs`: one outbound WebSocket to `wss://relay.withhide.dev/ws`, with the validated `HIDE_RELAY_URL` override for tests and development (plaintext `ws` is loopback-only).
The supervisor owns that socket and at most eight phone tasks; switching off, changing method, closing the move gate or shutting down cancels the link and joins its phone tasks.
Each peer has eight inbound frames, and the link has a shared 32-frame outbound queue; a full queue closes the affected peer with a content-free diagnostic.
Encrypted data and its routing close share that queue so the final refusal always precedes close.
Admission and sends have ten-second deadlines; each phone has one ten-second budget from arrival through Noise and its first credential message, and an unauthenticated connection never takes a paired-phone slot.
The link pings every twenty seconds and closes after sixty seconds without a response.
Each Noise receiver polls `check_timeout` once per second even without input; a ciphertext authentication failure, replay or unfinished chunk assembly closes only that phone and logs no content.
A lost link reconnects with equal jitter, from 0.5-1 second up to 15-30 seconds, with no retained transport retry queue.
The existing per-phone input request ledger survives link loss; input work runs beside the socket and is not aborted with it.
The blocking write itself owns a settlement guard, so cancellation of even its async waiter cannot leave a request permanently in flight; a panic settles uncertain.
The reconnecting phone reads the written, in-flight, refused or uncertain outcome without repeating an ambiguous write.
A method change waits for any Tailscale exposure in progress and its owned entry's removal before the relay can connect.
If the Tailscale CLI is gone, the obsolete ownership record is dropped and relay may connect, while the connection line retains the cleanup failure for the current daemon session.

Tailscale remains the advanced direct method, and `mobile/tailscale.rs` is the only file that knows its CLI.
It finds the CLI at `HIDE_TAILSCALE_BIN`, then the macOS app bundle's `/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale`, then `tailscale` on PATH, and reads `tailscale status --json --peers=false` for the backend state, `Self.DNSName`, `Self.HostName`, MagicDNS and `CertDomains`; every command runs with a fifteen-second bound.
The status is read without the peers because the full answer lists every peer at about 1.2 KB each (34 KB on a tailnet of 27, 3 KB without them) and would pass the 1 MiB a command may print on a tailnet of some 900, blocking Mobile; hided reads none of the peers' fields, and an answer past the bound is a failure that names the bound, never a cut one.
Every command carries `TAILSCALE_BE_CLI=1`: the app bundle's executable is both the app and its CLI, and it acts as the CLI only when its environment looks like a terminal (`SHLVL`, `TERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM` or `PS1`), which hided's never does, so without the variable every command started the app and timed out ([Tailscale CLI](https://tailscale.com/kb/1080/cli), macOS); the plain CLI on Linux and Windows does not read it.
Every command runs as an owned child under a 15 s deadline and a 1 MiB output bound (`OwnedChild::capture_until` in `hide-platform`, on a blocking task) and is answered when it has exited and its tree has ended, never when its output closes: on macOS a child another thread starts while the command's pipes are being made keeps the write end for as long as it lives (the platform layer's account of #729), and waiting for the output's end ran a command that had exited in milliseconds to the deadline, which failed a `status` read and, twice in a row, took the exposure down (with-hide/hide-private#524).
hided binds loopback as before and adds `tailscale serve --bg --yes --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, then confirms the entry with `serve status --json` before a QR is shown.
It records the entry before running the add, so an add that took effect and then failed or timed out is still recognised as its own on the next pass.
It refuses to expose while `AllowFunnel` covers that HTTPS 443 name, in the saved config or a foreground session's, because Funnel would publish the address to the internet, and says so on screen; a Funnel turned on after exposure takes hide's entry down and closes every phone until it is off.
A change of hide's own settings (the switch, the method) and the start each owe one pass, and a pass settles every change it read, so two changes that arrive before a pass starts run one pass and never a second one against Tailscale as the first left it; Settings opening and the clocks below force a pass because they ask Tailscale again (`PassOwed` in `hided/src/mobile/mod.rs`).
Settings > Mobile rechecks every three seconds while it is open, and with no one watching hided reconciles once a minute while Mobile is on, and while a removal is still owed after it was switched off, so a Tailscale that starts late is picked up and a failing command is retried at that pace; an exposed Mobile keeps its exposure through one failed Tailscale read and drops it on the second in a row, and a pairing code is minted only by `mobile_show_code` (Show QR), never by opening the tab, by a background pass or by a phone pairing; `mobile_hide_code`, the last Mobile page closing, and a pass that finds the code expired take it out of the frame.
It owns only the entry it recorded (`{dns_name, port, added_at}`): an HTTPS 443 handler it did not record is shown as the foreign target and left alone, an entry for its old port is replaced, and switching off or a clean exit removes it with `serve --yes --https=443 --set-path=/ off`.
Every start reconciles the record, so a crash's leftover entry is repaired or removed on the next start; `run_daemon` answers SIGTERM and SIGINT with the same shutdown, which removes the entry before the process exits.
A failed command leaves Mobile unexposed with the step that failed on screen, and its command line and stderr go to a `mobile_transport` record; a removal that fails at switch-off stays on screen and is retried until it succeeds, and shutdown waits for a reconcile already running.
While exposed, `https://<Self.DNSName>` joins the allowed WebSocket Origins, and only a phone handshake may use it; a desktop handshake from that Origin is closed with 4002.
A request that arrives through `tailscale serve` (a forwarded-for or Tailscale identity header, or a Host that is not loopback) reaches only `/m`, `/m/*`, `/assets/*` and `/ws`, everything else answers 404, and its `/ws` takes only a phone handshake from the Mac's tailnet Origin while Mobile is exposed, whatever other Origin it claims, with a 64 KiB frame limit.
Every handshake has ten seconds to send its first frame.

The core decides the phone list: `hide_core::agent_state::phone::project` returns the groups, and the phone draws them without sorting, nesting or cutting anything itself.
It reuses the sidebar's rules instead of a second set: the tree depth is `lineage::TREE_LEVELS`, a parent's children come from `lineage::children_in_order` (the parent's own child order, the most urgent `tree_rank` first, which the sidebar's `sidebar_tree` calls too, so the two cannot order siblings differently), the raised caps are `scope::RAISED_SHOWN`, and `lineage::SIBLINGS_SHOWN` is the five siblings per parent.
The core holds that last number once: it rides the snapshot as `navigator.siblings_shown`, and the sidebar, its popover and the Sessions tree in `web/` read it from there and raise when it is missing, so no TypeScript constant repeats it.
Groups stand in `turn::recent_first` order, the order `sort_agents` gives every surface.
`phone/tree.rs` builds each group from the rows of this Mac and of every connected device together, so one order covers them all, hangs a child under the parent that lists it (a delegated row whose parent is not listed is a root again; what lies deeper than the second level waits flat behind that row's `more_children`, so every agent stays on the phone to open or answer), and folds a group to its newest 5 (working and needs_you) or 3 (done and seen); the revisit group does not fold.
A group is `{group, count, rows, more, more_asleep}`: `count` is every top row including the folded ones, `rows` the shown ones and `more` the folded ones, each a tagged `agent` or `sleeping` row; a parent carries `children` (at most five), `more_children`, `children_open` (a descendant asks the operator) and `descendants {asking, working, done}`.
The frame also carries `devices`, this Mac and each remote with whether it is connected and its needs-you and working counts over top rows, which the header and the device sheet read.
A list frame (`agents`, `missions`) is one relay message, which `noise::MAX_MESSAGE` (256 KiB) bounds and past which the relay refuses it and closes the session, and both are in a connection's first frames, so a list that grew past it would close every reconnect again; each list therefore keeps within `phone::LIST_BUDGET`, the limit less 4 KiB for the frame's own fields, measured as the JSON it is sent as (`phone::FRAME_LIMIT`, which hided asserts equal to `MAX_MESSAGE` at compile time).
The agents frame's copy of the groups (`Projection::wire`) leaves rows out only when the whole list is over: folded top rows first, then the children of the rows left, then shown top rows, each the oldest first and group by group from the end of the drawing order, every other group before 내 차례, whose rows wait on the operator, so no row there goes while another group still has one; `count` stays every top row, `more_asleep` counts what `more` still carries, and the frame's `omitted` counts every agent left out, which the phone shows as one dimmed line under the list (`mobile.omitted`, the PR list's line) and hided records once per connection as `agents.capped`.
The projection itself stays whole, so notices and lookups never read the cut copy; a mission step whose worker's row was cut opens nothing, as one whose row the list does not hold.
The phone keeps only choices in its store (`childrenOpen` and `foldsOpen`, pruned to rows that still exist on each frame); it sends no event and moves no sidebar state.
The wire types are the `phone` module of `hide-core/src/agent_state/tally.rs`, `hided/src/mobile/phone.rs` puts them in the frame, `tally/phone/tree.rs` and `phone.rs` carry the tests that pin the shape, and the phone's `protocol.ts` mirrors it.

The phone app is a static shell and a data channel, kept apart.

`web/src/mobile/loader.tsx` is the small start page for `app.withhide.dev`; `web/src/mobile/main.tsx` is the same phone UI served directly at `/m/` and as a versioned relay bundle.
`pnpm --dir web build:phone` writes `web/phone-dist/`: the root `index.html`, `protocols.json`, root manifest and `/sw.js`, shared icons, and `/p/<PHONE_PROTOCOL>/index.html` with its own hashed assets.
`PHONE_PROTOCOL` is declared in `web/src/mobile/phoneVersion.ts` and, as the number the relay announces, in `hided/src/mobile/relay.rs`; the two are raised together, and only for a change an older side would misread.
It is 5: protocol 2 is the agents frame that carries the list as a tree (below), protocol 3 a page View's screenshot, protocol 4 the `prs` frame with the pull request requests (below), and protocol 5 the `html` kind of a View and its `look_head` mode (below).
A bundle opens only against a Hide that announces its own number, so every raise sends a phone whose Hide is a build ahead of the hosted site to the update screen until the next release candidate uploads that number's bundle; that is why an addition does not raise it.
An addition keeps the number and works in both directions:

- A new frame type is ignored by an older bundle (`applyFrame` in `web/src/mobile/store.ts` passes over a type it does not know), and a newer bundle draws the screen it feeds only once that frame has arrived, so against an older Hide that never sends it the screen stays away.
- A new field of an existing frame is optional: an older bundle ignores it, and a newer bundle reads its absence as this Hide not offering it.
- A new request is sent only from a screen or control drawn because of such a frame or field, so an older Hide does not receive it; one it does receive is answered `refused_request` with the request's type, and the connection stays open.

The number is raised when an existing frame, field or request changes shape or meaning: a field renamed, removed or retyped, a new value in a field whose older readers have no fallback for it, or a request whose older answer would be misread.
Each release candidate replaces its number's bundle with its own build, so the bundle under a number works against every Hide that announces that number.
Deployment retains older numbered directories and lists the available numbers in `protocols.json`.
Only main's release-candidate CI deploys that site, before preparing the desktop release; a failed phone upload or production check stops the candidate and therefore the private publisher.
[BUILD.md](BUILD.md#the-hosted-phone-release) owns retention, deployment secrets, CSP and the production check.
The root reads only the relay's `phone_protocol` metadata and opens that exact supported bundle, never a closest or newest fallback.
A paired device that is offline can open its saved protocol bundle and let the shared connection retry; a changed version returns through the loader.
An unsupported number stays on the update screen with the phone and device protocol versions.

`hosts.ts` owns one bounded browser storage record: at most sixteen paired devices, each with its room, plain-text display name, QR-authenticated Noise public key, credential, last protocol and last successful contact.
Corrupt records and storage refusal are visible failures; QR codes and conversation content are never persisted.
The QR fragment is cleared synchronously before WASM initialization and relay access; its name is escaped React text that wraps on the landing screen.
`relaySocket.ts` is the socket boundary used by the existing connection and command code: the shared WASM crate performs Noise NK, then the first encrypted message carries `{client_kind:"phone", pair}` or `{client_kind:"phone", token}`.
This boundary compares the relay's phone protocol with its own bundle before starting Noise, for both the main connection and every presence observer.
A mismatch closes without a handshake, credential or app frame; the main connection returns to the loader, while a list observer stops retrying and gives its row both versions and a loader action.
The direct `/m/` socket keeps its existing handshake and UI.
A relay socket owns its handshake deadline, chunk deadline check, and Noise memory; closing disposes all of them, and the browser send buffer is capped at 1 MiB with no retained application send queue.
Reconnection keeps the existing command request identities and adds jitter; no action is automatically replayed by the transport.
The host picker opens at most one extra read-only connection per other saved device only while its list is visible; it authenticates for counts but never opens an agent detail or sends an action.
The in-app scanner uses bundled `jsqr`, one camera and at most 640 by 640 pixels at four scans per second; hiding or leaving it stops every track and timer.

The hosted manifest starts at `/` so an installed app can add another device in its own storage.
The same `/sw.js` is registered once at `/` for the shell and once at `/push/<room>/` per saved device for push, since each device owns a different VAPID key.
Removing a device unsubscribes and unregisters its exact push scope before removing its credential; it never unregisters the root worker returned by an ancestor-scope lookup.
A notification retains the registration's room and opens `/?host=<room>&open=<device_id>|<pane_id>`, which selects the correct bundle and agent.
Only static responses and translated notification words are cached, never device data; the shell cache is bounded to 128 entries and old shell versions are removed on activation.
The app build embeds a strict CSP allowing same-origin scripts and `wasm-unsafe-eval`, same-origin assets, same-origin frames and the declared relay WebSocket; there are no external scripts, analytics, login or payment paths.
The one same-origin frame is `look-frame.html`, beside the bundle's page (`/p/<N>/` hosted, `/m/` on the tailnet), where an HTML View is drawn (below); it keeps a policy of its own, and the service worker leaves a frame's navigation alone so it never takes the app page's place in the cache.
`VITE_HIDE_RELAY_URL` is the only public build override: a credential-free WSS URL, or a loopback WS URL for isolated development.
Physical iPhone home-screen storage, camera and multi-registration push delivery require device verification; emulated viewport and service-worker tests do not prove those OS boundaries.

The direct Tailscale shell remains as follows.
`/m/` serves `mobile.html`, and `/m/manifest.webmanifest`, `/m/sw.js` and the icons come from `web/public/m/` through the same static route as the desktop shell's `/assets`; the page, the service worker and the manifest are served `no-cache`.
The service worker caches only that shell, so the app opens without a network and shows its unreachable line.
Pairing, the agent list, an agent's conversation, a pane's rows, replies, keys, starts and the push subscription travel on `/ws` only; HTTP fetches carry only static shell assets and the hosted protocol manifest.
The first frame decides the client: `{client_kind: "phone", token}` for a paired phone or `{client_kind: "phone", pair, name}` to pair; a phone counts toward `MAX_CLIENTS`, and a refusal sends `{type: "refused", reason}` (`code_expired`, `phone_limit`, `revoked`, `mobile_off`) and closes with 4001.
Every application frame to a phone goes through `mobile::phone::encode`; on a relay connection this calls the shared Noise session's `send_message`, including refusals and pairing credentials, and only ciphertext reaches the routing queue.

A pairing code is sixteen random bytes, is accepted only while Mobile is on and exposed, lives only in memory for five minutes, is spent by the first phone that uses it, and is replaced only when `mobile_show_code` is sent again; opening Settings > Mobile issues none and voids none (B58).
The relay QR is `https://app.withhide.dev/#pair=<base64url QR v2>`, carrying the device name, signing public key, Noise public key, derived room and code as specified in `RELAY_PROTOCOL.md`.
The advanced direct QR remains `https://<DNSName>/m/#pair=<base64url {v:1, endpoint, code}>`; neither code reaches a request line or a log.
A paired phone gets a 32-byte credential; `phones.json` (mode 0600) keeps only its SHA-256, compared in constant time, with the name, the last connection, the notification answer, the push subscription and its pairing scope (`PhoneOrigin::Relay` or the tailnet name).
The phone keeps the credential in its storage and in its address fragment (`#k=`), because the manifest has no `start_url` and a Home Screen app starts from the address it was added from, whose storage iOS may keep apart from Safari's.
At most four phones pair in one scope; the limit is checked before the code is spent.
Only phones in the selected relay or tailnet scope count (PRD mobile-relay B7, core-host-node-move B17): they are listed in Settings > Mobile, receive pushes and are let in, and the limit counts them; a switch-off or a failed check leaves that name as it was.
After a move the phone's Home Screen app still starts at the old machine's address, so each phone scans the new machine's code once; until then the phones paired where the core ran wait unlisted, a credential of theirs is answered `mobile_off` (the phone stays paired and shows the core as unreachable), and a move back lets them in again; the seven-day rule below ends them otherwise, so no more than four phones per address of the last seven days are kept.
Switching methods hides the other scope's phones without revoking them; switching back restores them.
`mobile.json` retains the last verified tailnet name separately from its owned Serve entry, so removing that entry or an offline Tailscale does not erase the direct phone list.
A record from before phones kept their address reads as `Unrecorded` and takes the exposure `mobile.json` names at the first load, or the first exposure.
A phone keeps at most two connections, the oldest closed first, a connection that answers no ping for 45 seconds is closed and recorded as `phone.silent`, and one whose frame cannot leave within ten seconds is closed and recorded as `phone.stalled`.
A phone away for seven days is revoked at start, by an hourly sweep and when it next connects, and a revoke, manual or automatic, drops the credential and the subscription in one write and closes that phone's connection.

A phone's whole vocabulary is `open`, `view`, `older`, `more`, `close`, `input`, `look_open`, `look_ack`, `look_seen`, `start_sheet`, `start_agent`, `answer_mission`, `ask_mission_material`, `reopen_mission_view`, `read_pr`, `merge_pr`, `read_pr_feedback`, `delegate_pr`, `wake_agent`, `wake_sleeping_session`, `check_sleeping_session`, `push_subscription`, `apns_registration`, `push_permission` and `ping`; anything else is answered `refused_request` and recorded as `scope.refused`, and a phone never receives a path, a setting or the core snapshot, and a file only as the content of a View that is open now and that it asked for by the View's id (next paragraphs); the one setting that reaches it is the interface language, which rides every `agents` frame as the core's stored value or null (the phone resolves it, and follows its own system language on null, before the first frame and when unpaired).
A phone looks at the Views of the agent whose detail it has open (`mobile/looks.rs`, PRD mobile-companion-ui D-06 to D-10, D-15, D-16).
The detail's task asks the core for the Views opened by that agent's session that are open now, in every checkout (`Core::agent_looks`, `view_sessions.rs::phone_looks`: newest first, one row per shown file, at most 64 with the rest counted as `omitted`), and sends a `looks` frame of ids, kinds by extension, names, whether each is unseen and when, and a web page's address, only when the list changed; a frame never carries a path, so a local page's `file:` address is left out.
`look_open` names an agent, a View id and a request id and nothing else; a View is found only among that agent's open Views, so the phone has no way to name a path, a root, another checkout's file or a View that closed.
A field beyond those, an agent the list does not hold and an id that is not open now are each answered `look_result` (`refused`, `gone`, `closed`) and recorded as `scope.refused` with `look_field:<name>`, `not_an_agent` or `view_not_open`; `phone.rs::look_scope` decides the first two and its unit test holds a path, a root, a checkout and a file among them, and `hided/tests/it/mobile.rs` sends the same over a paired phone's socket and sees no content come back.
The path stays in hided: the core's `LookView` carries it to the readers the desktop's `file_bytes` uses, `server::send_file_bytes` over this Mac's boundary and `server::stream_device_file_bytes` for a device's checkout (`device_root_known`, the same stamp checks), which write to a `FrameSink` so the one reader serves a socket and the relay's queue alike, and a path is confined to its checkout by the same checks for both.
The reply is `look_changes` for a diff (`changes::read` run on a blocking thread after `Core::prepare_checkout_changes` built its request in a short step on the owner thread; at most 200 files with their +/- counts and no code line; each row says `binary` when Git tracks the file and could not count it, and an untracked file, which the desktop's list shows no number for, has none), `look_result` `page` with its address for a web page whose screen cannot be taken now (the desktop's screen of it arrives as a `look_head` of mode `page`, below), `other` for a PDF, a video, another binary or a document that is not UTF-8 text, `too_large`, `closed`, `failed` or `device_unreachable`, or the bytes of a text document or an image.
Bytes travel as JSON text, because the relay carries nothing else: `look_head` (mode, size, chunk count, whether the cap cut it), `look_chunk` of 96 KiB as base64 and `look_end`.
A web page's screen is the desktop app's picture of it (`mobile/page_shot.rs`, PRD mobile-companion-ui B20-B22, D-11), taken by the path `hide browser screenshot` uses and not a second one: the core lists the View's checkout as a checkout caller (`checkout_caller_id`, no pane) for the display's area, kind and whether it is its area's selected View, `BrowserControl::relay` opens the registered desktop window's gateway (only this Mac's own window, a node's window answers "cannot be taken"), and `browser_page::still` attaches a `Page` with that selected flag and takes the visible viewport as a JPEG (`actions::still`: `require_visible` first, so a display behind another tab is `display_hidden`, then `Page.captureScreenshot` at quality 70 with the clip scaled to at most 1.5 million CSS pixels).
Nothing in the chain selects a View, moves keyboard focus or raises a window (B22); a View that is not in front is answered "cannot be taken now" and the phone never asks the desktop to show it.
It holds one `acquire_relay` slot for its whole life so a refresh storm cannot crowd out `hide browser` commands, is bounded at 20 s, and refuses a picture over the 10 MiB image cap.
It leaves as `look_head` of mode `page` carrying `url`, `taken_at` (ms) and `taken_by` (the device id of the Mac), then `look_chunk`s and `look_end` like an image, one at a time; the phone shows a head that lacks any of the three as a failed read.
Every refusal (`display_hidden`, `display_busy`, `window_elsewhere`, `timeout`, a closed display or an unavailable window) is one `look.page_unavailable` diagnostic with its reason and answers the phone `look_result` `page` with the address, nothing more.
A refresh is a new `look_open` for the same View id; the new one replaces the transfer in flight, so a repeated tap never runs two screenshots at once.
The wire of this is phone protocol 3.

An HTML file of a checkout is drawn by the phone itself, opened as a file or as a page (kind `html`, `mobile/html_look.rs`, with-hide/hide-private#689): a file View whose name the desktop's rule reads as HTML, or a page View whose `file:` address is such a file inside its checkout.
hided reads the page through the same readers, up to the image cap, then each file of the checkout it names by a relative address (`src`, `href`, `poster`, `srcset`, CSS `url(...)` and `@import`, found by a scan rather than a parser) and what its stylesheets name, while they fit under that cap and 64 files, and writes each back into the text as a `data:` address; an address on the internet stays as written, a file outside the checkout is never read, and what is missing or past a limit stays as its address and is counted once as `look.html_files_left`.
The folded document leaves as a `look_head` of mode `html` and its chunks like any read, `too_large` when the folded document passes the image cap.
The phone draws it in `look-frame.html` (`web/public/m/look-frame.html`), loaded `sandbox="allow-scripts"` without `allow-same-origin`, so its scripts run in an opaque origin that reaches none of the app's storage, credentials or connection; the frame says it is ready, the viewer posts it the document, and the frame writes it over itself.
The frame's policy lets a generated page run inline and CDN scripts, styles and fonts and its `data:` files, and refuses `connect-src`, forms, frames, workers and plugins, so nothing it runs talks back; the hosted release serves it with that policy as its header and `frame-ancestors 'self'` ([BUILD.md](BUILD.md#the-hosted-phone-release)).
The wire of this is phone protocol 5.

Text is capped at 1 MiB (the first 1 MiB, with `truncated`) and an image or a folded HTML document at 10 MiB (refused from the size the first frame reports, so it is never read whole).
The relay closes a peer whose 32-frame queue fills, so a transfer is paced by the phone and never by a timer: at most four chunks are ahead of the last `look_ack`, one transfer runs per connection, a new `look_open` replaces it, and it ends with the detail or the connection.
The phone puts the chunks back in order and refuses a head over its cap, a chunk out of order or more bytes than the head said (`web/src/mobile/lookContent.ts`).
`look_seen`, sent once the phone drew an answer about the View (its content, or a name, a kind or an address where there is none to show; not a loading, closed, failed or unreachable screen), marks the View seen through the Desk's own seen-by-id event, `desk_output_seen`, dispatched on a blocking thread like every other phone dispatch, since a dispatch waits on the core's owner thread, the same one its lane sends (D-15); the core accepts that one event while Desk is off, because a View's seen state is the core's and not Desk's.
A document or image on a device is read only while the device's helper is linked (`CoreHandle::node_link` first): a device that is not answers `device_unreachable`, as its change list does, and a read that fails after the link was up answers `failed`.
The phone's list puts an agent with a View not seen in Needs You as the desktop's does (`PhoneAgent::group`), and notices keep following the group it would have without the View (`PhoneAgent::notice_group`, D-13).
A web page's screen is the web-shot node's work; until then its row opens to the address.
A page cannot see the protocol-level ping hided sends, and a Mac that went to sleep leaves the phone's socket open until the phone's operating system gives up on it, which can take minutes, so the phone checks hided itself (`web/src/mobile/connection.ts`, `phone.rs::liveness`).
A slow pane write (a reply or key to a device pane can wait out an SSH channel open) runs beside the socket loop like a start, so a `ping`, an eviction or a revoke is never held behind it: one input per connection is written at a time, a second is answered `in_flight`, and the write is not aborted when the connection ends because its request id must still be settled (`phone.rs::spawn_beside_loop`).
`ping` carries a number and hided answers `{type: "pong", id}` from one in-memory admission check, with no core lock, no engine call and no read of the list; a phone no longer let in is sent `refused` with its reason instead, and a `ping` without a number is refused and recorded as `scope.refused`.
The phone keeps one timer per connection and counts any frame from hided as proof it is there, so a phone that is receiving never pings: after 20 seconds of silence it sends `ping` and gives hided 10 seconds to send anything, then closes the socket from its own side, without waiting for the browser's close, shows the unreachable state and retries as for any loss.
A silent hided is therefore shown as connected for at most 30 seconds after its last frame; returning to the foreground or regaining the network sends a `ping` at once with the same 10 seconds, and a hidden page asks nothing.
A new socket that says no `hello` within 15 seconds is given up the same way, so a retry toward a sleeping Mac does not wait for the browser's own connect timeout.
A phone starts an agent through the same `agent_start_in_checkout` event as the desktop (`mobile/start.rs`, PRD home-device-rail D-24, D-25), marked `stay_behind`.
`stay_behind` is the one word that tells the core the start did not come from the operator's own screen: the task slot keeps it (`TaskOperationSnapshot::stays_behind`, never sent to a shell), `ingest_task_operation_result` then leaves the terminal, the keyboard focus and `selected_pane_id` where they were, and the tab request asks the engine not to focus the tab it makes (`CheckoutTabRequest::focus`, the same `focus: false` a branch migration sends).
The tab is made and listed as for any start, so the new agent appears in the sidebar and in the phone's list, and the phone opens its detail from that list; ⌘N, New worktree, an issue's Start and the desktop card's pull request hand-off send no such word and keep bringing their tab forward; the phone's hand-over of a pull request sends it (below).
While its start sheet is open (`start_sheet`), hided sends it a `start_catalog`: every device's checkouts as targets named by id, the core's machine's system (`core_platform`, from its device row's `host.platform`) for the phone to name that machine in its language, `claude` and `codex` with the models the provider catalog lists, and the choice the last start remembered; the sheet counts as a start surface for the catalog demand, and the folder a target id leads to stays in hided.
`start_agent` carries a request id, the text, a target id, a kind and an optional model; it is refused before anything is dispatched when the phone is no longer admitted or the target, kind, model or text is not one the sheet could have sent, and otherwise answered with `start_result` once the core's task slot or last error carries that request id, or `timeout` after 90 seconds (`start::ANSWER_LIMIT`, the core's own limit for a start).
A request id the phone repeats is started once: the repeat gets the first answer, joins it while the first still waits, or, after a `timeout`, follows the same start again without sending it; one connection waits for one start at a time, and a second is answered `in_flight`.
The list is `agent_state::phone::project` over the snapshot's `rest` section (`agent_state/tally.rs`, called by `mobile/projection.rs`): the local navigator's agents and every connected device's, in the desktop's four groups, each keyed by device id and pane id with its lineage root.
The core supplies each phone group’s order and count; the phone renders both without recounting.
Sleeping conversations are separate safe rows in that projection, carrying only their `SleepId`, provider, title, canonical group, phase, age and action availability.
They carry no native session, cwd, former pane, close key or lineage, and can never open a pane detail or receive input.
A phone may wake or inspect only a currently projected local sleep intent, with an exact-key payload and renewed phone admission before dispatch.
Its correlated `sleep_result` acknowledges dispatch only; the core-owned row supplies progress or refusal, and a lost answer never triggers an automatic resend.
hided follows the core only while Mobile is on with a phone paired or a desktop window has agent notifications on, reads the snapshot off the core lock with its own cursors once per notification burst, and republishes the list only when it changed.
A detail shows the agent's conversation (`mobile/conversation.rs`) or its terminal, as the phone chooses with `open` and `view`, and hided reads only the one shown, once a second and only while it is open.
Claude Code and Codex draw in the alternate screen, so the pane holds no scrollback for them and a pane read returns only the screen; the conversation comes from the agent's own transcript instead, found through `hide-session` from the session the engine reports for the pane.
Only a pane on this Mac with a reported session whose adapter supplies conversation has one: a device's transcript is on the device, and the newest transcript in a pane's folder may be a neighbour's, so every other pane sends `{type: "conversation", state: "none"}` and shows its terminal, and so does a pane whose session has written nothing yet.
A page is the newest 30 messages, or 256 KiB of their text, before a byte cursor, read backwards in 512 KiB windows (`hide_session::read_page_before`) and never more than 8 MiB a request; the offset of its oldest message is the cursor `older` sends back, and the phone keeps at most 300 messages.
What the agent appends is read the same way down to where the last read ended, when the file's length changed, so a transcript line of any size is passed over rather than stopping the reader; a catch-up past 8 MiB, or a file that shrank, sends the newest page again.
Cursor pages follow native turn and step references backwards under the same 30-message, 256 KiB text and 8 MiB read limits; polling follows its graph checkpoint rather than database length, so a same-length native append is observed and a rewritten prefix resets the page.
An older Cursor pager requires its retained source stamp to remain current, and every page and idle poll repeats native owner and checkout proof.
