One search runs at a time (`GithubSearchWork`): a request with the running search's request id or query joins it and starts no second worker, any other request becomes the single pending one and replaces an older pending one, and it starts when the running search ends; the slot shows the latest request as `working` at once, and an answer whose request the slot no longer shows is dropped when it lands, as `ingest_issue_detail` does.
A failed call, any repository's, fails the whole search with the slot code `github_search.failed`, which the palette words, and a `github_search.failed` diagnostic that carries the request id and the real reason; a worker that panics is a failed search too, so it can never leave the one search slot taken.
`create_worktree` with a `task_key` writes the link into the new worktree's metadata after its identity is confirmed, and a `prompt` goes to the agent as its first prompt (above); a prompt the encoder refuses fails the agent start, and the task operation carries why.
The GitHub adapter reads what the existing GitHub reader already fetched off the lock (`github.rs`); every local Git project is read already, so the Overview's 백로그 and the sidebar's 태스크 list only send `github_request` for the projects they show, with `refresh` naming a project to read it again and `look` (sent by `web/src/githubLook.ts` when the window gains focus or a project comes to the front) asking only for a read when the last answer is 30 seconds old, and a read that fails keeps the last tasks with the failure beside them.
The GitHub adapter also reads each open issue's `blockedBy` in one `gh api graphql` query per pass, grouped by repository and at most 20 blockers per issue, and keeps only open blockers as `blocked_by` (a key and the id this repository shows); `gh issue list --json` has no dependency field.
Each issue's labels (name and colour) come in the same `gh issue list` answer and, for an issue read by number, in the same query (`labels(first: 100)`), so a card's labels add no request; they ride the task as `labels` in GitHub's order, a colour that is not six hex digits is no colour, a Local issue has none, and the wire leaves the field off when it is empty.
The same query reads each issue's `subIssuesSummary { total completed }` and `subIssues(first: 100)` (GitHub's limit per issue), so sub-issue progress adds no request and no polling; `total` and `completed` ride the task as GitHub counts them, and the web finds a sub-issue's pull request among the project's `pull_requests` by their `closing_issues`.
A dependency query that fails or answers with `errors` is a failure, never an empty answer: the pass keeps the issues it read, restores the blockers and sub-issues read before, records `issue_dependencies.unavailable` in the diagnostic log, and states the failure on the task source.
A local Git project's catalog row also carries `pull_requests`, the ones the PR list, the Project tool and the card show (PRD overview-lenses-prs D-32, D-52, work-tab-pr-lens, sidebar-task-lens): the open ones and the merged ones whose worktree record is still here or that merged in the last 14 days, taken from the `gh pr list` answer `github.rs` already holds, so the view adds no read and the row stays bounded by that list's cap; the field is left off the wire when empty.
The list is two `gh pr list` calls at the same time, every pull request without its checks and the open ones with only their checks, and a merged or closed pull request keeps the checks read while it was open or reads `Unknown`, except that one settled in the last 15 minutes with checks last read pending or failed has its head commit's checks read again (`github.rs::list_pull_requests`, `recheck_settled`; [status-model.md](status-model.md#github-status-in-the-workspace-row)).
A pull request is tied to a checkout in one place, `github::pull_request_for_checkout`, which every surface asks (the sidebar row, the worktree catalog, an agent row's request block, `pr_link_issue` and `pr_delegate`): an open one by head branch unless it comes from a fork, a merged or closed one only at the checkout's exact HEAD (`CheckoutSnapshot::head_sha`), because a branch name reused for new work must not show the old merge; `refresh_worktree_projection` decides it again when a catalog read moves a HEAD.
`head_sha` is the commit the worktree reader already holds, so no Git process or file read joins the lock.
Until that reader first answers, and for a checkout it never lists, the commit `Repository::head_oid` read from Git's own files stands in (`CheckoutSnapshot::head_oid`, core only), so a merged pull request restored from the saved answer reattaches in the first frame instead of after the reader's first pass; the reader's value wins as soon as it exists, because it reruns on a moved HEAD or ref while the file value is only as new as the row's last build.
`head_oid` and each repository's remotes (`PathFacts::remotes`, the `[HOST/]OWNER/NAME` each `remote.<name>.url` names, unknown when the config includes another file or a remote names a server in a form the node does not read, such as `http://`) are read by the core's own node with the catalog's other path facts (`Call::PathFacts`, `hide_host::catalog::path_facts`), which the coordinator asks off the lock before it builds the catalog, so `build_catalog` and the reconcile under the lock compare names and read no folder; a runtime the coordinator does not feed (a fixture, startup before the engine answers) asks its own node before it takes anything from the session, and the `packed-refs` read behind it is streamed and capped at 8 MiB, with no process.
`build_catalog` places every path that reaches it, a pane's directory and a registration alike, by one rule (`workspace::Places`): the node's answer first; then, for a path the node cannot place, such as a linked worktree whose folder was removed while an engine workspace still holds a pane there, the deepest checkout holding it that Git's worktree list or the engine names, the engine by the checkout it attached the workspace to and that checkout's `repo_root` (`workspace.worktree`, carried as `SessionSpace::checkout` and asked of the node with the panes' directories); and only a path none of them places is a folder of its own, never placed by the shape of its name.
Of several registered folders that hold a pane's directory (a project inside the home folder project), the deepest places it (`deepest_holder` in `hide-core/src/runtime.rs`, the pane's engine workspace deciding only between equals; PRD home-folder-project D-07), and the same rule picks a checkout within the project (`runtime/session.rs`), labels a session in `hide session` (`project_holding` in `links/session_command.rs`), gives a session its retention (`LinkStore::prune`, `deepest_owner`) and a path its registered root (`Boundary::strip_root`); a pane in a folder no project holds sits under the home folder project once it is registered, instead of a temporary row.
A directory in no repository is placed by the deepest registered folder of its node that holds it (`Places::registered_folder`, and `device_catalog::held` for a device's folders), ahead of an owner mark, so a pane in `~/notes` is the registered home folder's and makes no row of its own; the owner mark stays the engine's binding of its workspace.
The disk sweep leaves out the home folder (`sweep_project`), which the core knows by the real path a node reports as `Hello::home_real` (its own `home_real` for this machine); the node's `home_folder` answer to a measurement stays the defense.
`IndexService::set_roots` drops the file index of every root that holds, or sits in, a root that came or went, so a home project's list follows the projects registered inside it; a project already in the catalog that is only registered later keeps its list until a query after the list is five seconds old starts a refresh and it lands.
Such a checkout stays a row of its repository with `exists: false`, and a registration that resolves into an already registered repository is not a second row; a repository's own registration names its project before a registration of one of its checkouts can adopt the row.
A device's catalog follows the same rule from its helper's answers (see Device catalogs).
The coordinator establishes catalog ownership before its first ingest and runs path facts on a `BackgroundRead` worker, so neither the first answer nor a refresh holds topology publication.
Each local `PathFact` also retains the native `hide_project::facts` result for Memory scope resolution, read by that background owner with the same path budget.
A path whose Project cannot be read, or whose root the wire cannot spell because it is not UTF-8, is answered without Project facts and with the reason (`PathFact::project_unread`), which the core logs as `project_facts.read_failed` from the path reader that asks that node on every refresh, once per path until its reason changes; the reader keeps only its latest answer's unread paths, so a path no longer asked is forgotten and a path another node answers is never mixed in; the rest of the reply stands.
The hook and analysis therefore hash the same canonical native root, including Windows spelling and Folder file-to-parent resolution; `/` comparison paths retain only their catalog matching role.
An older or unreadable fact without Project data refuses the Memory scope instead of inventing a different durable ID or starting discovery from the hook.

There is one active read; changed paths coalesce to the latest request, whose connection and wanted paths fence the answer.
Agent and PR display metadata cannot invalidate path facts when the wanted paths are unchanged; current registrations and the worktree catalog independently fence the prepared catalog at its final Runtime application.
A completed answer wakes the existing coalesced republish channel, and the catalog is built from the current session rather than a captured session.
Until facts arrive, an existing tab retains its confirmed checkout and a new directory creates no project row; failure retains accepted facts and goes to diagnostics.
The reader checks owner cancellation between bounded path chunks and joins its current finite node call when the coordinator ends.
A repository's files are written by whatever runs in it, so each (`HEAD`, a ref, a pointer file, the config) is opened only when its name resolves to a regular file, without waiting on a pipe, and refused past a cap (a pointer at 64 KiB, the config at 1 MiB).
Discovery takes only a repository whose own `HEAD` is a regular file, as it always has; the files read after it (a ref, `packed-refs`, the config) follow a link as Git does, so a config a dotfile manager links in still names its branches, and one that resolves to something other than a regular file reads as `branch_notes.read_failed`.
A row the reader never lists keeps the file value for at most the catalog's 30-second refresh after its HEAD moves.
`PullRequestSnapshot::head_oid` and `cross_repository` stay in the core and are never sent to the shell.
Hide writes to GitHub with exactly four commands, all behind the exact-shape allowlist the core's own node checks before it runs `gh` (`hide_node_link::gh::allowed`) and all on a worker thread off the lock: `gh issue create --title T --body B` (a new issue), `gh pr edit N --body B` (a pull request's body, and nothing else of it), and the PR card's two, `gh pr merge N [--merge|--squash|--rebase] --match-head-commit SHA` and `gh api --method PUT repos/OWNER/NAME/pulls/N/update-branch -f expected_head_sha=SHA`.
`pr_link_issue` links pull request N to an issue of the project's source: a Local issue is Hide's link alone (the branch's issue link and the Workspace token, through the same task-operation write as the issue link), a GitHub issue of the same repository is that link plus `Closes #M` written by `github::write_closing_line`, which reads the body with `gh pr view N --json body` just before and writes nothing when a closing keyword already names the issue, so a retry never adds a second line; `new_issue` makes the issue first and keeps it when the body write then fails.
`pr_feedback_read` reads a pull request's body, failed checks and standing change requests in one `gh pr view N --json body,statusCheckRollup,reviews`, for a new issue's fields and an agent's first prompt; `pr_delegate` starts an agent with a prompt on the pull request's head branch, in its checkout with `agent_start_in_checkout`'s path, or with none through the engine's worktree creation on that existing branch, fetched from origin first when only origin has it (`worktree_control::spawn_existing_branch_worktree`, the fetch under the same bounded Git runner), so a new branch is never made; a node project's branch is checked over the node's link and its worktree made by the node's engine.
Each answers in the snapshot's `pr_work` slot (`link`: the step, `create`, `link` or `body`, its phase and the issue made; `feedback`), or, for the start, the task-operation slot every start reports through; a later request replaces the slot, and a failure is also a `pull_requests` diagnostic.
The fields are additive and none is a string enum, so the shell decodes the snapshot as before.

The PR card (PRD work-tab-pr-lens, sidebar-task-lens D-43, D-50) is four events and one slot.
`pr_open {workspace_id, pr_number, checkout_id?, open_workspace?, at?}` is the one event that opens a card: it puts the card in front of the 보기 slot (`ui_state.detail`, below) that `at` names and starts the card's read, `owner` (what the web sends from a place with no agent) bringing the pull request's own agent forward when it has a pane on this machine, `{pane}` (an agent's row) that pane, and `here` (the default, a card in the slot) leaving the Workspace, its Agent tab and the keyboard where they are; with no owner on this machine the slot in front takes it; with `open_workspace`, sent from Home, the core also chooses the Workspace (the checkout of the pull request's agent, else of its branch, else the project's primary) and brings the pull request's live agent forward unless a pane was pressed, so the web sends one event and the screen is never half moved.
There is no `PR #N` display in File Views any more; a card a file saved as a View is dropped as `workspace-views.json` loads (`workspace_views::drop_retired_cards`).
`pr_card_read {workspace_id, pr_number, look_again?}` reads what the five-minute list does not carry in one `gh api graphql` query (`hide_node_link::gh::pr_card_query`, an exact shape the allowlist names by owner, name and number): the head commit, the body, the first 100 files with additions and deletions, the first 50 review threads, the repository's allowed merge methods, whether it has a merge queue on the pull request's base, the viewer's permission, the repository's `.gitattributes`, the head commit's first 100 checks and the last 50 reviews, from which the card's timeline takes when the checks completed and when the standing review was given (`hide-core/src/github/card.rs`; PRD pr-card-and-session-record-redesign D-04).
The helper allows only the query text it knows, so the fields moved the node protocol to 39 and a helper on 38 is refused at Hello and reinstalled.
A part that cannot be understood is named in `failed` and the others stand; files that `.gitattributes` marks `linguist-generated` or that are a common lock file are flagged `generated`.
The slot is `pr_work.cards`, at most eight cards (`PR_CARD_LIMIT`), the least recently opened dropped first, and a read already running is not started twice; the operator's Look again (`look_again: true`) dismisses a failed write notice and reads the list too, while a plain `pr_card_read`, the card's own reads and the read the core starts itself after a moved head keep the notice.
A merge with a method that GitHub accepted, made from this machine's own project, reads as merged at once (`Runtime.merged_here`, `read_merges_made_here`): the list shows it merged with the time it was seen until a fresh read says merged, closed or gone, or ten minutes pass; a read that failed releases nothing. A node's project and a merge-queue ask wait for the list, as before.
`pr_merge {workspace_id, pr_number, head, method?}` and `pr_update_branch {workspace_id, pr_number, head}` are the only GitHub writes the card asks for; each is one worker call, a second ask while one works is the same intent and is not sent again, and the head is the commit the card showed, so GitHub refuses a pull request that moved (`--match-head-commit`, `expected_head_sha`).
The answer is a code, never GitHub's text: `head_moved` (and the core re-reads the list and the card), `conflict`, `not_mergeable`, `denied`, `unreachable` or `failed`, with `already_merged` counted as success so asking again writes nothing twice; the detail goes to the `pr_write.failed` diagnostic.
A card's AI summary rides the same slot (`docs/AI_PROVIDERS.md`).
A project on a connected node reads and writes through that node's `gh` (`github::Where::Repository`), and a project a core does not read opens GitHub in the shell instead.
The reads the list gains for the PR list are in `docs/status-model.md`, GitHub status in the Workspace row, and the groups the core decides from them in Pull request groups.

A Workspace's right lane (PRD lane-two-columns B1, B17, D-09: whether it is `open`; whether its viewing column shows the checkout's `documents`; its tool column's one `tool`, `project`, `memory`, `explorer` or `changes` (History), null while there is no tool column; whether it is `pinned` beside Agent Views; and the four widths, `document_width` for the documents, `detail_width` for the 보기 slot, `explorer_width` for the Explorer and `panel_width` for the Project tool, Memory and Changes) and the arrangement of its View areas belong to the core (S6 D-10, S7 D-11), keyed by device and checkout path in `hide-core/src/workspace_views.rs` and kept in `workspace-views.json` beside `core-state.json`, a versioned file of its own so neither the old settings nor the single-surface editor state is rewritten.
Only `hided` names that file (`CoreOptions.workspace_views_path`), and it always does; without it the core keeps the earlier single-surface editor, and none of the View area keys below reaches the snapshot.
The file keeps at most 256 Workspaces (`MAX_WORKSPACES`), and making one past that forgets the one used longest ago: an entry is used when the operator chooses its checkout (`last_used_unix_ms`, which also names the checkout a restart resumes) and when it is made (`made_unix_ms`), so a checkout nobody has opened yet, such as a project just added, keeps its Agent tabs rather than being forgotten first and drawn as an empty start screen over its live terminal.
The shell sends one `workspace_view` event for the lane, a column, the pin, a width or a reveal (`open`, `documents`, `tool`, `pinned`, the four widths in CSS pixels, and `reveal`, a file of the front Workspace, checked by path components like any file read, whose folders unfold in the Explorer in the same event); every field is the value it should end at, so the same event sent twice lands where it did once, and the snapshot's `workspace_view` is the front Workspace's entry; it is absent from the wire when no Workspace is in front.
`open: false` closes the lane whole and keeps its columns, pin and widths, the front pane's 보기 slot still `shown`, so `open: true` brings the same columns back, the slot included, while any other call into the closed lane (a `tool`, `documents: true`, a reveal, an area intent or the slot coming forward) opens it on that call's column alone, the other column closed and, for a tool, the slot left on the rail, and for the slot no documents under it (`WorkspaceView::open_on`; operator decisions 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24); `detail_close`, and a `detail_back` or a dropped item that empties the slot, leave `documents` as it stood under the slot, so the viewing column goes back to the documents only when they showed before the slot came forward; `open: true` on an entry with no column and no shown slot shows the documents when the checkout has a display and the Explorer otherwise (B15); `documents: false` or `tool: null` closes that column alone, the lane closing when neither is left (`has_column`, B12, B14); `documents: true` and `open: true` are calls, numbered in `lane_called` whether or not the field moved, and only `documents: true` leaves the 보기 slot (`leave_detail`, B10); each call records the column it brought forward (`lane_called_side`, `view` for an open, the slot or ⌘E, `tool` for a tool, a reveal or a folder link), which a lane too narrow to draw both columns draws in front (B19); `detail_show {shown: true}` while the slot is already shown opens the front checkout's closed lane (`open_front_lane`, B22); a `reveal` turns the tool column to the Explorer and opens nothing (B8); a `tool` the core does not know is refused (`workspace_view.unknown_tool`), and a width is held to `1..=8192` (`clamp_width`), the shell keeping each at its minimum.
Whether an unpinned lane floats over the agents now, and whether it is expanded, are the shell's own moment and are never sent or stored.
The widths stay absent until the operator first resizes a column, so the default lives in the shell's tokens rather than in the operator's file.
Keyboard width intents also carry an optional `width_request_id` (1 to 128 bytes), which the core echoes in the Workspace snapshot from one bounded runtime slot keyed to its Workspace; it is never stored in `workspace-views.json`.
Each mounted divider retains one pending absolute target, calculating a later key from it until its own acknowledgement arrives; an older acknowledgement from that divider cannot retire the newer target, and another caller, changed geometry, focus loss or unmount rebases it on the core's frame.
The shell still draws only the core's widths and sends one idempotent absolute-width event per key; acknowledgement-only changes publish without saving unchanged widths, and there is no timer, request queue or per-key subprocess.
The operator's close of the last view (`view_layout` close, after the save it waits on) closes the viewing column (`close_emptied_lane`, B12), the lane with it when there is no tool column, while an agent's `hide view close`, a cap's eviction or a document closing elsewhere changes no lane field; an open from the front pane, by any route (an Explorer pick, ⌘P, a page, a `hide` open from the front tab, or a terminal link once it settles in that Workspace), sets `documents` and numbers a call, and leaves `tool` as it is in an open lane (B6).
The Project tool is written to the schema 5 file as `project` and Memory as `memory`; a schema 4 file loads whole, its `memory` tool read as the Memory tool it is again and its `prs` tool as no tool column, since that one is not migrated (PRD lane-two-columns D-10; operator decision 2026-10-23), and the earlier `work`, `agent_sessions` and `prs.only_checkout` keys are not read.
The global `ui_state.right_panel_visible` and `right_panel_section` are projected from the front Workspace's tool column: Changes and the Explorer as their sections, the Project tool and Memory both as `Memory`, which no reader gates on (`Overview` would start the disk and Git reads), and no tool column as hidden, so the Changes reader and the device Explorer watch keep the one gate they had.
The lane's 보기 slot (`hide-core/src/runtime/detail.rs`) is the `ui_state.detail` of the pane in front: `ui_state.detail_pane` names that pane, the one with the keyboard in the tab the front Workspace shows, and the slots of the other panes are `ui_state.detail_panes`, the one seen longest ago first, at most `DETAIL_PANE_LIMIT` (64) with the oldest leaving first, both core only and saved with it; `sync_detail_pane` swaps the front pane's slot in whenever another pane comes in front, so the wire and every reader see one slot (operator decision 2026-11-09, replacing one slot per Agent tab). It holds `items`, a pull request's card, a session's record or plan, a mission's map, or a project's worktree table (`worktrees`) or cost (`cost`), the last two drawn from the snapshot and the usage frame with no read of their own, at most `DETAIL_HISTORY_LIMIT` (20) with the oldest leaving first, and `shown`, whether the lane draws it. The slot belongs to the pane, never to a tab, a checkout or the window: another pane in front, of the same tab or another, a shell's included, shows its own slot or an empty one, and an agent woken in a new pane finds that pane's empty slot. `detail_open {item, at?}` and `pr_open` carry `at` (`DetailPlace`): `here` (the default) the slot in front, `{"pane": id}` that pane's slot, the pane taking the keyboard in the same event (`open_detail_in_pane`), and `owner` the pane of the agent that owns the item (a record's or plan's session, a mission's Conductor, a pull request's first agent; `detail_owner_pane`), so one press is one event; a pane no catalog lists or an owner with no pane on this machine leaves the item in the slot in front. A device's pane comes forward only when the device answers, so `{pane}` on a device puts the item in that pane's kept slot, opens the lane of the pane's Workspace and asks the device to focus the pane, and the slot swaps in when the device's session reports the pane in front; an owner on a device is not looked up. A kept slot goes with its pane: `prune_detail_panes`, on each session from this machine's engine or a device, drops the slot of a pane its catalog no longer lists, and a swap does not keep the slot of a pane that closed; a pane of this machine is judged once the navigator lists a pane and a device's once its session is here, so a launch before the catalog arrives or an offline device drops nothing and the first session after a launch drops what closed meanwhile. The per-tab slots an older build saved (`detail_home`, `detail_tabs`) are not read: the front slot, saved as `detail`, attaches to the pane in front on the first event, and the rest leave the file on the next write. The work `sync_detail_pane` adds to every event, terminal input included, is one lookup of the front pane, and on a move to another pane one search of the at most 64 kept slots and one look at whether the pane it leaves is still listed; it is saved in `core-state.json`, and `detail_open`, `detail_back`, `detail_close` and `detail_show` each start or stop the read of what it shows on the same event.
The sidebar's `ui_state.sidebar_lens` (`projects`, `tasks` or `prs`, the last drawing the board's rows for the device, PRD lane-two-columns B41) and `task_view` (`status` or `project`) sit beside it; `sidebar_lens_set {lens, show?}` turns the lens and, from ⇧⌘B with the sidebar hidden, shows the sidebar in the same event, `ui_state.sidebar_project {device_id, workspace_id}` is the one project both the 태스크 and PR lists show, set by `sidebar_project_set {project, lens?, show?}` (a 현황 tile turning the sidebar to its list in the same event), rekeyed by a core move through `node_migration::KEYS` and forgotten when the project is unregistered, and `task_reveal {pane_id, session?}` shows the 태스크 list on that row unfolded and opens its record in the slot.
Practice mode's progress is `ui_state.practice`, chapter id (`^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$`) to `{version, step, finished}` (the chapter version played, the step reached, at most 255, and whether the end was reached), set one chapter at a time by `practice_progress_set {chapter, version, step, finished}`, kept for at most 64 chapters and saved with the rest of the UI state, where an entry a build cannot read is dropped and the rest load, and an entry under an id no flow names (the dropped `plan` flow's) stays as saved, is never shown and sends no statistic; a refusal is `practice.chapter_invalid`, `practice.step_invalid` or `practice.too_many`, and a write of the value already held changes nothing.
The sidebar's invitation to practice closed with its × is `ui_state.practice_invite_closed`, set by `practice_invite_close` (no payload), never cleared, kept by a whole-state save that still reads it open, and saved with the rest of the UI state.
The Overview Work map's choices (`hide-core/src/model/overview_graph_choices.rs`) are `ui_state.overview_graph`: the filter, Include sleeping, the hidden and folded projects, the teams folded or opened by hand, and the dropped places of projects and sessions per map scope, each record naming its machine, project and pane in its own fields so a core move rekeys it through `node_migration::KEYS`; `overview_graph_change {change}` carries one operator action (`focus`, `project_hidden`, `project_folded`, `fold_all`, `unfold_all`, `team_folded`, `place`, `reset_places`), every list keeps at most 512 records with the least recently changed forgotten first, and a stored record the build cannot read is left out on load while the rest loads (PRD overview-graph-remembered).
The 태스크 list draws the device's `agent_scope.tasks` (each task's root, members, checkouts and state, in the core's order, `hide-core/src/agent_state/tally/tasks.rs`) through `web/src/TaskLens.tsx` and `web/src/taskList.ts`.
Its visible-board demand reuses the existing running-checks observation gate rather than adding a polling worker or clock.
Session escalation, resolve and pane headers are pure core projections over accepted agent, delivery and PR facts (`agent_state`, `runtime/session_state.rs`).
Changed inputs refresh the projection under Runtime and publish only changed values; repeated transport-control frames do not rederive headers.
Resolve uses the existing coalesced state-save worker and publishes its durable result after the save answers; the end of the Resolved window compares one deadline on the existing coordinator tick.
Remembered sidebar folds survive incomplete startup and reconnect catalogs, as recent checkouts do, and leave only with a confirmed project or device removal.

That projection is never saved: `core-state.json` keeps the right panel it held when the process started (`ui_state_to_save`), so an older build started on the same state directory opens with its own panel.
A new Workspace starts with its lane closed, so it shows Agent Views alone.
An unpinned lane floats over Agent Views and a pinned one docks beside them (D-02, D-03): the pin turning on or off, a docked lane or one of its columns opening or closing, a docked divider landing and a docked viewing column turning between the documents and the 보기 slot when their widths differ resize the agents' terminals once (lane-two-columns B21), and a floating lane, a drag in progress, an open inside the lane and an agent choice resize nothing.
The file is schema 5 (`StoredLane`, whose tool names are `project`, `explorer` and `changes`); a schema 4 file is read whole with a `memory` or `prs` tool as no tool column, and a schema 3 file (`StoredOneToolLane`, the one-tool lane), a schema 2 file (`StoredColumns`) and the schema 1 shapes before them, whichever build wrote them, read once on load with the lane's fields at their defaults, closed at the default widths, and the documents, splits, groups and comments as they were (lane-two-columns B23, D-10): the old `tool`, `last_tool`, `tree` and widths are not carried over, because the one operator starts from the default shape rather than keeping a migration path.
Such a load records `workspace_views.migrated`, the next save writes schema 5, and a file of a schema this build does not know is kept aside with a diagnostic and the defaults.

The same schema-3 entry keeps its original `agent_layout` as the ungrouped tree and adds defaulted `agent_groups` and `agent_starts` fields.
`agent_groups.rs` owns at most 32 named collections, their independent area trees, the selected collection and explicit Hide draft identities; an older entry loads with every existing tab and its original split tree ungrouped, without converting tab names into groups.
The collection's durable `initialized` flag separates its first real topology from a deliberately empty selection: a checkout whose initial topology contains only delegated tabs opens their first canvas without adding a strip tab, while later arrivals preserve empty groups and drafts.
When lineage resolves a selected ordinary tab as delegated after that first topology, reconciliation preserves the same canvas while removing its strip slot.
Names are trimmed to 1 to 80 Unicode characters, reject controls and line breaks, and must be exactly distinct within the checkout.
Create, rename, move, dissolve and undo are one core event (`runtime/agent_groups.rs`); they change membership without moving or restarting the engine's PTYs.
An ordinary selection clears its area's delegated canvas override; moving a lineage root prunes only overrides whose canonical group ownership changed, and explicit child navigation reveals its root's current group.
Dissolve appends the group's ordered tabs to the ungrouped active area and retains one session-local undo record, invalidated by the next group mutation or unloading the checkout's saved state and never serialized.
The selected group's layout is projected for local, inbound-node and outbound-SSH checkouts; outbound SSH keeps one area and depth zero per group, while local and inbound-node groups keep six areas and depth three.
The core retains the explicit remote checkout choice independently of a device's raw engine focus, so selecting an empty group or draft can navigate without creating or focusing a PTY.
An unanswered session or unresolved checkout catalog preserves groups and drafts; authoritative topology reconciles live membership only, admitting ordinary external arrivals to ungrouped.
A node's tabs reach its areas when its session arrives (`reconcile_node_agent_topology`, through the same `reconcile_agent_topology`), the tab of the area in use is asked of the node's engine (`focus_node_tab`), the node's own focus moves the area in use (`sync_agent_selection`), and the panes of every area's tab attach as the front tab's do (`node_shown_agent_tabs`).
New Agent tab requests use `agent_group.new_tab` with `terminal: true` and reuse the existing local or device tab-control queue, without entering the agent-start operation or waiting for shell integration.
The control captures the selected group and area before admission, and its creation answer places the native tab there even if the operator changes groups meanwhile.
When the authoritative catalog arrives before the answer, that answer reconciles its captured placement against the full known checkout topology before the visible tab can choose a group from membership.
An unanswered catalog or a tab not yet listed keeps the existing pending placement; a newer group choice, including an empty group that sends no engine focus control, keeps the screen while the created tab joins its original group.
Local requests retain the existing bounded input holder until the new pane can receive keys.
Device terminal intents reserve the same display and pending-placement capacity before sending, with distinct admission identities and the existing request replay guard.
Restore and replacement effects share that pending budget, and an unreserved fork or legacy result cannot consume capacity promised to a pending terminal.
The pending checkout choice grants a created device tab focus only until the operator makes another visit; a later placement retains the newer tab and area fronts.
Older clients and saved drafts retain the draft-start transition.
Externally created ordinary tabs join the ungrouped active area's bar without replacing the selected group or shown canvas, including when creation focuses the new tab in the engine.
The engine's session carries the creation cause and a focus revision with the authoritative workspace focus (`SessionTabFocus`).
One pending creation pairing per live tab is consumed by the first move onto that tab; a later move gets a new revision and is followed.
The engine records no move for a focus command that leaves its shown tab unchanged; Hide cannot observe that no-op command.
This metadata remains inside the core projection, adds no terminal-output work, and is removed with its tab; local New and Reopen intents retain their existing focus claim.
Each Workspace stores one Files View list, `view_layout`, with its split, selection and active area, independent of Agent tabs.
Obsolete `tab_views` bookmarks and the older per-tab keys are ignored; the existing `view_layout`, lane, documents, comments and Agent layout are retained, without a schema change.
The shell receives the existing projected layout and Agent switches make no View-selection change.
A focused View close follows the core-selected successor only after the removed display leaves the snapshot.
The shell retains one bounded pending follow and rejects it after newer input, disconnection or a Workspace change.
Desktop window activation is reported separately from native page focus, so a page taking input never makes the app appear inactive.
The lane's tool, pin, tree and widths stay checkout-wide.

Workspace control records the caller's actual tab and native session before an asynchronous read, validates them again at commit, and refuses stale identity without another-tab fallback.
`caller_stays_behind` decides who is a background caller.
On the front Workspace, every caller but the pane the operator is in (the selected pane, `snapshot.terminal.pane_id`, or a device's focused pane) is: another pane of the same tab, and a checkout-bound shell, which no pane vouches for.
On a Workspace not on screen, a pane of a tab other than its active one is (B7); the active tab's panes and a checkout-bound shell change only what that Workspace shows, so a page they open is selected and can be driven.
A desktop window's browser gateway never is, because a page its CDP client creates loads only in front; hided names it `gateway:<key>:<path>` (`gateway_caller_id`), which `Caller::parse` reads as a checkout caller with `gateway` set, so it resolves like any checkout caller and is told apart only here.
No command option makes a background caller foreground.
A background command records the selection first (`keep_front`) and puts it back after the commit (`restore_front`): a new display stays at the end of the area it landed in, in no area's front, and the area in use, the keyboard and the editor's active tab are as they were.
An open or select from the foreground caller calls the lane on Files after the commit, decided before the open adds its view so a tree that showed alone stays beside it; a browser page's own area-bound target calls nothing.
Reconcile, preview retirement, close guards, restart hydration and browser inventory read the checkout's one list.
Admission counts the checkout's 32 displays (`MAX_VIEW_DISPLAYS`) in its six View areas.
An open that would pass the cap first closes the display focused longest ago in the checkout (`make_view_room`); the search skips every area's front and never closes a document that holds work or a file still being read back; a display that was its document's last closes that document as `close_file_tab_now` does, and each close is one `view_layout.oldest_closed` diagnostic.
Each layout retains depth three, and authoritative Agent topology keeps the existing 64-tab admission and prunes closed records.
The same admission check covers a caller on an inbound node; an unanswered session or unresolved catalog grouping preserves saved state, while an empty checkout in a fully answered catalog prunes its final tab's pending reads.
Pruning drops a closed tab's pending reads and keeps its displays and clean documents in the list, so a tab close never closes a View.
Every tab-valued owner and tab-keyed map participates in `node_migration::KEYS` with `Moves::Tab` for core moves and returns.
Changes use the existing coalesced off-lock save and notification path; identical state creates no additional save or publication, and there is no new polling, subprocess or blocking work under Runtime.
Agent admission counts the shared checkout-wide 64-item limit across every group's drafts and live tabs together with pending creates, placements, reopen and replacement-close effects.
Request-specific claims reserve slots before the worker starts; reconciliation places acknowledged local effects before external arrivals and does not expire uncertain claims by time.
An ambiguous local create gets one bounded marker lookup outside the runtime lock, without another mutation; an unresolved claim remains charged for that runtime session.
Reopen and replacement claims have the same explicit owner, independent of operation phase or Dismiss; retries reuse their claim, and a confirmed tab transfers it to placement before the claim is released.
A close retry that reuses a confirmed replacement carries reuse-only permission to its worker, so a concurrent deletion cannot turn that retry into a new creation.
An authoritative excess tab remains in checkout topology and contributes to the snapshot waiting count; reconciliation admits it when a slot opens without selecting an unplaced tab.
Hide refuses a new external effect at capacity, including a protected replacement close, and uses the existing capacity notice surface.

`split_tree.rs::SplitTree<I: AreaItem>` owns structural repair, ordered membership, focus, move, split, collapse, resize and limits; `view_layout.rs` wraps it with document/preview/browser rules, and `agent_layout.rs` wraps it with Agent tab references and delegated canvas selection.
`agent_groups.rs` composes those Agent layouts without duplicating their tree rules; draft identities are explicit Hide state and never the engine's topology identifiers.
The shared web `AreaTree` consumes View and Agent adapters over `areaLayout`, `areaDrag` and column-scoped drawn frames, so gestures, geometry, dividers and narrow presentation have one implementation.
`AgentTab` renders the same status/provider/name/Rename unit in every area, and `PaneCanvas` receives its explicit tab.
Agent actions name the Workspace and group and use the shared stale-frame guard and bounded split-request deduplication; only authoritative topology reconciles persisted live references, so a startup placeholder cannot erase the saved tree.
Created and reopened tabs carry their group, area and position into reconciliation; a removed group falls back to ungrouped and a removed area to that group's active area.
The snapshot's `workspace_view.agent_layout` contains the selected tree, group identity and membership metadata; `checkout.tabs` remains the source of real tab and pane contents, while explicit drafts render their start surface without inventing a pane.
Only the selected group's shown live tabs enter the shown-tab attachment set, including an authoritative empty set for an empty group or draft; hidden groups add no attach work or polling and the existing recent-tab cap still applies.
Group changes leave the checkout's `view_layout` and each real tab's `tab_views` bookmark with their existing owners.
Every new real-tab or pane reference in the groups, receipts and closed-item records participates in node migration; Hide's draft identities remain distinct from those rekeyed engine identifiers.

Schema 2 of that file (PRD S7) stores each Workspace's View areas as a binary split tree (`layout`, rules in `hide-core/src/view_layout.rs`).
A split node has an `axis`, `row` for first-left and second-right or `column` for first-top and second-bottom, and a `ratio`, the first child's share, clamped to 0.15..0.85; a leaf is an area holding its displays in tab order and naming its `active` display.
A display is one tab showing one file or diff (`path`, `kind`, `committed`, `preview`, `last_focused_unix_ms`) or one web page (`kind` `browser`, with its `url` and the `title` the page last reported), and the Workspace names its `active_area`, the one it last used, where the next file opens.
Area, display and split ids (`a<n>`, `d<n>`, `s<n>`) are minted by the core from the layout's `next_id` and never reused in that Workspace, so an id in an event names one thing for the Workspace's life; a Workspace with no layout has one empty area `a1`.
The same invariants hold on load and after every change: an area has at most one preview display, its `active` names one of its displays or is null when it has none, an empty area exists only as the root, `active_area` names an existing area, and the caps hold.
Loading repairs a file that breaks them in one pass over the tree per rule and reports what it changed as counts in one diagnostic, and a file whose ids or focus stamps come near the end of their numbers, which only a crafted file can, is renumbered, keeping what each area shows and which view was focused last, so minting never overflows.
The caps are core constants, published in the snapshot as `layout.limits`: 6 areas in the checkout's layout (`MAX_VIEW_AREAS`), 3 split nodes on the path from the root to any area (`MAX_SPLIT_DEPTH`) and 32 displays (`MAX_VIEW_DISPLAYS`), which is also the tree's own cap.
A split that would pass the areas or the depth is refused with `view_layout.limit` and its reason, an open that would add the 33rd display when no display can close (see above) is refused with `view_layout.display_limit`, a browser open included, and nothing changes; an open of a document that is already displayed is a focus and is never refused, and a file that carries more than the caps is trimmed on load with a diagnostic, never on an operator's action.
The display cap holds on every path: a preview open beside a preview whose document holds work (which stays and makes the open an addition), Reopen Closed, a file the Explorer creates and a revealed file are refused before anything is read or made, a read that lands after the views filled is refused as it lands (a Reopen Closed then keeps its item), a layout change that adds a display past the 32 is refused, and the tree's own operations refuse a 33rd display, so nothing can pass it.
A schema 1 file (S6) migrates once: its tabs become the displays of one area `a1` in their saved order, its active tab becomes that area's active display, its preview flags are kept, its lane starts closed, and the next save writes schema 5.
Any other version, a file that does not parse and a migration that fails all take the S6 path: the file is renamed aside as `<name>.unreadable-<ms>`, the defaults load with a `workspace_views.unreadable` diagnostic, so nothing is resumed and the page starts on Main, and when the rename fails the store is frozen so nothing is written over the original; saves are atomic and run on a worker, coalesced, never under the runtime mutex.

A display never holds a document.
It binds at runtime to the S5.5 editor tab, the one buffer per device, checkout and document (the tab id, `editor_documents` and the save pipeline), and any number of displays may bind the same tab, so two views of a file share one text, one dirty state and one save queue rather than copies that could diverge (S7 D-03).
Those displays can sit in different Workspaces: a terminal link to another checkout's file binds a display of the front Workspace to that checkout's tab (A clicked path is one event).
Closing a display that is not its document's last removes the display alone, and a `pending_save` sent with it is not needed; closing the last one runs the existing `file_close` path, save-then-close with the carried `pending_save` and the conflict protection, so a document leaves only once its buffer is safe.
The web's frame may still show another view of a document the core already holds in one, so a close of the last view of a dirty, saving or failed document that carries neither `pending_save` nor `discard: true` (the operator's Don't Save) is refused as `view_layout.unsaved`, naming the document, and nothing changes.
A document that becomes dirty, is saving or has a save state promotes every display of it in the same event, because a preview is replaced by the next click and such a document must never be.
In web mode the per-checkout preview slot of `place_editor_tab` gives way to one preview display per area: a preview open retargets the active area's preview display in place, and its old document is retired when no other display shows it, like the preview replacement before it, with no Recent Closed entry; the single-surface editor fallback keeps the per-checkout slot.

A browser display binds to nothing (issue 155, [BROWSER_DISPLAYS.md](BROWSER_DISPLAYS.md)): it is `open` from the moment it exists, the reconcile never removes it for want of a document tab, and a restore reads nothing for it.
`browser_open` from the Explorer or a page's new tab places a display in the named Workspace or the front one, a page's new tab beside the page it names (`beside_display`): in the area next to the page's, else in a new area to its right; pane CLI requests use the separate scoped Workspace action.
`browser_state` records the address, title, and native load state a page reports, while `view_layout` `navigate` loads the operator's own address.
UI `browser_open` receipts remain in `status.browser_opens`, where the shell reads the one an operator's open named to hand that page the keyboard (BROWSER_DISPLAYS.md); pane CLI requests receive their own scoped action result.
A load stamp (`load`, never saved) is how the core asks the desktop app to load a display's address again, and the address, capped at 8 KiB, holds only `http`, `https`, `file` or `about:blank`; loading repairs a stored display that breaks this to `about:blank`.
An `external` display binds to nothing either: it holds an outside file's grant, name and viewer kind, is `open` from the moment it exists, is never stored, and its `html` kind is listed among the inventory's `browser_views` with an empty address so the host keeps its page (A clicked path is one event).
A browser display with no `url` is the shell’s new-tab page, creates no native page, and is never deduplicated with another empty display.
A file open captures the active empty display with its placement before reading; it replaces that exact display on success only while it is still empty, and a diff selection uses the same placement rule.
A build from before browser displays reads a file that holds one as a file that does not parse, and so takes the unreadable path above: the file is renamed aside and the page starts on Main.

A layout change is one `view_layout` event whose `action` says which: `focus` (a display becomes its area's active display, its area the active area, and its `last_focused` is stamped), `focus_area` (keyboard focus moving between areas), `move` (a display to an index in its own area, which reorders, or in another existing area, where a display of the same document gives way so no area holds one twice; either way the index is the display's final place, counted without that twin), `split` (a display into a new area at one `edge` of an area, taking half of it), `resize` (a split's ratio), `close`, `keep_open`, `retry` (an unavailable display's file read again) and `navigate` (a browser display's address).
Each is one operator action and one frame, and it applies to the front Workspace only; a moved or split display becomes its area's active display and that area the active one.
Every payload names its Workspace as `workspace: {device_id, path}`, copied from the `workspace_view` of the frame the operator acted on, because ids like `d2` repeat across Workspaces and the front can move between that frame and the event; an action naming any other Workspace changes nothing and leaves a `view_layout.stale_workspace` diagnostic with both Workspaces and the action, and no screen error, since the screen already shows the other Workspace.
Every action may arrive twice, so each converges: `move`, `resize` and the two focuses carry their target state, `split` carries a `request_id` whose repeat among the Workspace's last 32 (kept in memory only) changes nothing, and closing a display that is already gone is a no-op with a diagnostic.
An unknown id is refused with `view_layout.unknown_*` and its reason, and so is a split that would change nothing, a display split away from an area it holds alone.
A move or close that empties an area collapses it in the same event and its sibling takes the space; the last area stays, empty.

In web mode `file_open` places a document this way: one already displayed in the front Workspace focuses its most recently focused display, and pins it when the open is not a preview; otherwise a preview open retargets the active area's preview display, or appends one when the area has none, and an ordinary open appends a pinned display to the active area.
`file_open` with `beside: true` is Open to the side: a pinned display of the document in the area next to the active one (right, then left, then down, then up among the tree's neighbours), a new area to the right when there is only one area (within the caps), the empty area itself when no view is open, since an empty area is only ever the root, or a focus of the display already in that area; when that split is refused as the read lands, a display of the document already open is focused, and with none the open is refused with the split's reason rather than doubled up in the area it was asked from; it rides on `file_open` so the request still crosses hided's path boundary like any open.
`changes_select` places diff displays by the same rules, `file_keep_open` pins every preview display of its document, `file_focus` focuses its most recently focused display, and `file_close` closes every display of it and then the document through the existing guards.
`file_draft` and `file_conflict` carry the `tab_id` of their document, which the web always sends, because with several documents on screen the active one is no longer necessarily the one that was typed into.
Opening, restoring, renaming, closing and removing a device create and remove editor tabs by paths the layout does not see, so after every event the core reconciles the two: a display whose document tab is gone is removed, and an editor tab of a restored Workspace that no display shows gets a pinned display in the active area.
Terminal input and output and a document's keystrokes (`file_draft`) skip that pass, since they move no area, and every snapshot read runs it first; a first edit keeps its document's displays open in its own event, looking only at its own Workspace.
Reads land on workers, so two can land with no event between them, and an open reconciles before it places its document: otherwise a preview it replaces could still be unbound from the restored document it shows, which would then come back pinned beside the new one.
The reconcile holds the display caps too: such a document of a Workspace that already has 32 views waits off screen, is reported once with a `view_layout.display_limit` diagnostic, and shows once a view is closed.

With the regions separate, choosing an Agent tab no longer takes the editor off screen: `editor.active_tab_id` is the document of the active area's active display, null while that display is not open (`front_active_view_tab` in `runtime/view_areas.rs`, applied by the reconcile), where before every terminal choice deactivated it.
The core also owns when the lane is called (PRD right-lane D-13, `apply_area_intent_to`): an explicit file open, History selection, page open, Recent Panels display, or a CLI open or `view select` from the operator's own pane shows the documents (`AreaIntent::Documents`), and a `workspace_view` `reveal` (Select in File Tree) or a link that names a folder turns the tool column to the Explorer (`AreaIntent::Explorer`; lane-two-columns B6, B8).
Choosing an agent or a tab changes no lane field; a status change, a hover or a menu opening moves nothing, and a refused event moves nothing either.
Each such intent, and every `workspace_view` that names a tool, is numbered (`lane_calls`, the count in any Workspace) and the number is kept as the called Workspace's last (`lane_called`) with the column it brought forward (`lane_called_side`: `tool` for a tool, a reveal or a folder link, `view` for an open, the 보기 slot or ⌘E), all on the snapshot's `workspace_view`; the shell reads them to put an unpinned lane up and, in a stacked lane, to draw that column in front (B19), so a call from that page, the CLI or another page reaches it the same way, and a call into one Workspace never moves another's lane.
The numbers are runtime only and never stored, since whether an unpinned lane is up is the page's alone.
The call history follows the Workspace store's 256-entry retention and is forgotten with a removed device.
Choosing a Workspace or an agent on another device than the one in front is one event: `focus_checkout`, `focus_tab`, `focus_pane` and `remote_control` carry `focus_device`, and the core brings that device forward only when it accepts the request, so a refusal leaves the device in front where it was.
A Recent Panels commit of a display in another checkout is one `focus_checkout` naming it by `display_id`: the core checks the display is in that checkout's Workspace before moving anything, brings the checkout forward, opens its lane on Files, and makes the display the one in use; an unknown display refuses the whole event with `view_layout.unknown_display`.

The snapshot's `workspace_view.layout` is the front Workspace's tree with its `active_area`, `limits` and `display_count`, each display carrying its `tab_id`, `label`, `kind`, `committed`, `preview` and `state` with an optional `reason`; `editor.tabs` still lists every document.
A restored Workspace's tree, ratios, tab order, preview flags, active displays, active area and lane are published the first time it is in front in a process, before any file is read, so the layout appears whole rather than tab by tab.
Each display then moves through its own `state`: `waiting` while its Workspace's root cannot be read yet, with a `reason` naming the device state (`Waiting for <device> to connect` while its helper connects), then `opening` while its read is in flight, a Retry's read included, then `open` once it is bound to a document or diff tab, or `unavailable` with the read failure as its `reason`.
A device helper that cannot be used, one refused for its protocol, unsupported, on a changed identity or not allowed, gives the device's own reason, the one History and Settings show, and its displays keep `waiting` so they open once the device is fixed; Retry on a waiting display is refused with that reason.
The wait is `view_root_ready`: on this machine a read waits until hided has opened the checkout's root, and on a device until its helper is ready and its catalog has moved its checkouts into their Projects (`ingest_host_established` and `refresh_device_catalog` ask again), because a read before the helper is refused and would mark every file unavailable, and a restore before the grouping names a Workspace the device no longer shows.
A restore opens into the Workspace in front, so it runs only while that is still the Workspace the last sync recorded; a front that moved since waits for the sync rather than filling one Workspace with another's files.
The reads land in any order and each fills its own display in place, because the order lives in the stored tree rather than in the order the documents arrive; S6's recording of tabs in strip order, and the reordering once the last read landed, are gone.
A Workspace records nothing into the file until its restore has landed, so a Workspace whose files cannot be reached, or a quit before the reads land, keeps the layout it saved.
An unavailable display keeps its place with Close view and Retry, `retry` reads its file again or, for a diff, opens its diff tab again, and every other display and area is untouched; nothing is started in the engine, no split or zoom is replayed, and a terminal layout changed meanwhile wins.
A diff display stored without its Changes group is repaired on load to the working group, so it binds to the diff tab its restore opens instead of standing beside a second display of it.
Unsaved text returns through the web's per-document draft reconcile in IndexedDB (S5.5), never through this file.
Removing a device forgets its Workspaces' entries, and a pending save is joined when the core is dropped, so a change made just before quitting is on disk.

Two kinds of state stay in the web and are never dispatched.
A drag's preview (the floating tab, the insertion line, the edge overlay with its label) is local, and only a valid drop sends one `view_layout` `move` or `split`; Escape, a drop outside, an ineligible or vanished target and too little room send nothing, and nothing is resized or saved during the drag.
Whether a lane is expanded (`laneExpanded`) is decided in `ui.ts` and never sent or stored; whether it is up is the core's `open` alone, so Escape on an unpinned lane sends `open: false` as ⌘E does, and the next tool or open into it shows its own column alone (`WorkspaceView::open_on`; operator decision 2026-10-23, replacing the page-local put-away state that kept the core's lane open and its readers running behind it).
The lane is called through the core's numbers alone (`readCalls` in `web/src/workspace.ts`, read on every snapshot by `web/src/laneCalls.ts` whether or not the Workspace screen is drawn): the front Workspace's `lane_called` past the `lane_calls` the page read last is a call, so a call older than the last read never moves a Workspace chosen later, and a lower `lane_calls` is a core that started again; so the page never applies its own open twice; another Workspace in front shows its lane as its stored tool says.
A file a terminal link reveals is numbered on its own checkout's Workspace once it settles there (`settle_reveal_path`), a linked folder too, and an intent that numbers a call announces the snapshot even when nothing else moved.
The page's one dispatch choke point (`laneCalled` in `web/src/actions.ts`) records which column a `workspace_view` that opens the lane, names a tool or the documents, or reveals, and a linked folder's `reveal_path`, brought to the front (`stackFront`) for a lane too narrow to draw both; an agent or tab choice and a press on a terminal pane leave the lane, and Escape inside an unpinned lane or on its rail (`laneEscape` in `web/src/WorkspaceScreen.tsx`) closes it.
What the body draws is `laneFrame` in `web/src/workspace.ts`, from the core's entry, the page's moment, the body's width and the tokens alone (`--size-agent-views-min` 480, `--size-lane-min` 360 and `--size-lane-ideal` 520 for the documents and the 보기 slot, `--size-tree-min` 180 and `--size-tree-ideal` 240 for the Explorer, `--size-lane-panel-min` 360 and `--size-lane-panel-ideal` 400 for Memory, PRs and Changes): the mode (closed, overlay, docked or expanded), Agent Views' width, the lane's, and each column with its stored `field` and width (`LaneColumn`), the viewing column's `document_width` or `detail_width` and the tool column's `explorer_width` or `panel_width`; the viewing column gives up width first and the tool column after (`fitColumns`), a pinned lane docks only while Agent Views keep their minimum beside both, else floats with `narrowPin`, and columns that cannot stand side by side stack, the page's `stackFront` drawn (`stacked`, B19).
Agent Views and the lane are drawn in one row under the full-width toolbar (`LaneRow` in `web/src/WorkspaceScreen.tsx`) with the rail after it: a docked lane leaves an empty slot of its width beside Agent Views, and the lane itself is positioned over that slot, over Agent Views' right edge, or over the whole body, so changing between floating, docked and expanded never remounts it; Agent Views stays mounted under an expanded lane, `inert`, so its terminals neither park nor resize, and the page records the keyboard owner from focus and pointer events, including native page focus from the desktop host, to route a chord, the lane's tool owning it inside `[data-lane]`.
A lane out of sight stays mounted, `invisible` and `inert`, so its documents, tabs, scroll and pages keep their state, holds no Escape layer, and hands the keyboard to the focused pane when it held it; the documents stay mounted the same way while the 보기 slot stands in front of them, while they are folded and while a stacked lane draws its tool column, laid out at their own width so their View areas measure what they will show, and a browser display's slot hidden this way hides its page without closing it.
A divider (`web/src/LaneDivider.tsx`) drags a guide and sends one `workspace_view` with the width it lands on: the lane's divider sends the width of the column at the lane's edge, in that column's `field` (`laneLanding`), against Agent Views, and the column divider trades width between the two columns in one event so the lane and Agent Views keep theirs (`columnLanding`); a browser display's slot reports its rect like any other, and a resize that lands reaches the page through the slot's ResizeObserver.
A lane drag belongs to its starting Workspace and geometry; changing either, or unmounting its divider, releases its pointer capture, listeners, guide and shell-drag mark without landing a width in another Workspace.
The web also owns the pixel rule, because it has the geometry: an edge takes a drop, and a Split item or an Open to the side from the only area is enabled, only when the target area's size along the split axis is at least twice `--size-workspace-area-min` (a `row` split) or twice `--size-view-area-min-height` (a `column` split) plus the divider, and the split stays within `layout.limits`; the core owns the counts and the depth and refuses whatever passes them.

A pane's delegated children and ancestors come from the global machine-qualified pane rows the core projects (`children.chips`, `lineage_path`; rules in `web/src/lineage.ts`).
The remote session preserves a declared raw pane and machine id, and the runtime scopes it only after the consented helper greeting supplies that device's immutable machine identity.
A parent's header opens the tree popover from its tree button, a child's header draws its ancestor path, and the pane menu lists parent, siblings and children.
Each explicit Open follows the same tracked navigation as the sidebar and Sessions; Escape returns to its badge, and the tree popover's `개요에서 보기` opens the Overview at the agent's task.
Each of those moves is one `focus_pane` carrying a `request_id` (on a device, `remote_control` with `report_pane_focus_outcome`), and the core's `status.pane_focus_request` is the only answer the header shows: pending until the engine's layout confirms, or failed with the core's reason and Retry when it can be retried; a second click on the same target while one is in flight is dropped, and a failure never splits the parent or makes a pane.
On a device, a delegated child whose owner group the core cannot resolve (its agent registration ended, so no row names its root) still opens: the Agent area selects that tab in the group in front and logs `agent_layout.owner_unresolved`, rather than answering the device's acknowledgement with a request that succeeded and a screen that did not move.

### The `$HOME` filesystem boundary

`hided/src/boundary.rs` is the one place the boundary is enforced, in the dispatch path before an event reaches the core (`server::apply_boundary`).
A `create_workspace` names a folder inside `$HOME`, or an existing folder outside it that the operator confirmed (PRD wsl-device D-02, D-10); any other path (a `..` segment, a symlink under home whose target leaves it, a file, a missing directory, a relative path, home or a folder holding it, an unconfirmed folder outside home) is answered to that client as a `path_refused` frame with a reason code (`outside_home`, `needs_confirmation`, `home_root`, `project_holds_home`, `not_found`, `not_a_directory`, `invalid_path`), logged as `path.refused` with the path capped at `LOGGED_PATH_CAP`, and never forwarded.
The rule is one function, `hide_host::register::judge`, which hided calls with this machine's home (`Boundary::resolve_registration`) and a device's helper calls with its own (`Call::Registrable`), so the two never drift apart.
Where a path stands against home is judged by file identity, not by its text (`hide_platform::fs::identity::below` and `holds`): another spelling of home or of a folder holding it, such as macOS's `/System/Volumes/Data/Users/<me>` or `/System/Volumes/Data` itself, another letter case on a volume that ignores case, or a link to home, is home, not outside it.
A path under home is resolved one component at a time from home, where a symlink's target is tested as written before it is followed (`SYMLINK_HOPS` bounds the chain), so an escaping symlink answers `outside_home` whether its target exists, is a file, or is missing, with or without a confirmation.
A path outside home is answered `needs_confirmation` until the event carries `confirmed_outside_home` naming the project it would add, compared as a path after the same `~` expansion and shape checks: that project's root, or the folder itself when it is the root. An unconfirmed request is read only as far as naming that root, which the answer carries as `confirm` when it is not the folder as written, so the operator is asked once, about what would be added; a folder that is missing or is not a folder is asked about as written, so only a request that confirmed it learns why, and a confirmation of any other path, a parent or a child included, asks again.
A confirmed path is then answered by what is there (`not_found`, `not_a_directory`, `invalid_path` for a loop or a denied folder); a folder holding home (`/Users`, `/`, `C:/`) is `home_root` before and after it is read, a folder in a Git repository whose root holds home (dotfiles kept in `~/.git`), or home itself when it is that repository, is `project_holds_home`, since the project it would add is home, and a Windows network path (`\\server\share`, `\\wsl$\...`) stays `outside_home`, whether it is written or a link on a drive leads there, since a network share is no project's identity (D-15).
Home itself is asked about, not refused (PRD home-folder-project D-01, D-02): by identity (`hide_host::register::is_home`, so a link to home or another spelling of it is home too) it is answered `needs_confirmation` with `home: true` (`Unregistrable::ConfirmHome`, `HostError::home`, carried to the shell on `path_refused` and on `last_error`), and it is registered as a plain folder project only when the request carries `confirmed_outside_home` naming that same path.
An agent's `hide ~` (`project_open::admit`) never carries the confirmation, so it is refused `needs_confirmation` unless home is already registered, when it only brings the project forward; a pin of an unregistered row whose folder is home is refused the same way by the row check (`ingest_row_registration`), and nothing else registers it.
Nothing stores that a project is the home folder: the Explorer listing (`hide_host::list::list`), the file index walk (`hide_host::index::walk`), and the disk measurement (`hide_host::disk`, which answers the home folder's row with no total and the code `home_folder`) each ask the host's own home by identity, so a device's home project is judged by that device's helper.
At the top of a home project the Explorer and ⌘P leave out names starting with `.` and the system's app-data folder (`list::home_clutter`: `Library` on macOS, `AppData` on Windows), for tidiness and speed and not as a guard, since a typed path or a link still opens them, and the index walk also skips every other project's registered folder (`Call::Index { others }`, asked of the core's registrations on the walk's worker), whose files ⌘P finds in their own project; the caps stay.
A registration adds the project its folder belongs to, the repository's root (its main checkout's, for a linked worktree), so a folder inside a repository outside home, a linked worktree of one, and a worktree under home whose repository is outside it are answered `needs_confirmation` with `confirm` naming that root, the dialog asks about the root, and only the root's confirmation registers them.
Nothing keeps a confirmation: the registration is the permission, so `Remove project…` takes it away and adding the folder again asks again, and the Explorer's file work on a registered folder outside home is confined to its checkout root exactly as one inside home is.
No other path registers a folder outside home without that answer: pinning a row the engine shows without a registration, and the registration that keeps a project listed when its last pane closes, ask the row's machine the same question with no confirmation (`Call::Registrable`, off `Mutex<Runtime>`), register only what it accepts, and otherwise leave the row unregistered, which a pin reports as `workspace.pin_refused.needs_confirmation` and a close only logs (`row.unregistered`).
An accepted workspace path is forwarded as the canonical path that was checked.
A `remote_file_list` names a path on a remote machine, which the boundary knows nothing about, and is forwarded untouched, a `local` target included, which names no device and which the core answers as an unconfigured target; the core lists it through that device's helper (`node_access::list_folder`), the same confined listing the web Explorer gets, though a remote target's own registration file panel has had no shell sender since the native shell that carried it was removed.
A device with no consent answers that panel with the `not_allowed` file state and a message naming what allowing installs and runs; the panel shows it with an Allow control that sends `device_host_consent`, and the core lists the panel's root again once the helper is ready.
A `file_list` is the Explorer's line for one folder inside a checkout the user already registered: the path has to resolve under that root (a folder that leaves it, or a root that is not registered, is answered `outside_checkout`) and the listing carries files as well as directories, keeps dotted names, and drops `.git` alone.
Those rows follow `hide_host::list::natural_cmp`'s order - directories first, then a case-insensitive name comparison in which a run of digits compares by value - and are capped at `LIST_CAP` with `truncated` set.
The `$HOME` line lists nothing itself: on the window's own machine Add a project picks its folder with the desktop app's native picker (`hide:pick-folder`), so hided only judges the path it is handed, and the one `directory_list` it answers is the Explorer's, named in `kind`.
Add a project's own folder list, for a device, a browser tab and the core's machine seen from a node's window, is a `home_folder_list` {device_id, path} that hided never judges or forwards to the core: it asks that machine's node (`core.node_link`, `Call::HomeList`) on a thread of its own, off `Mutex<Runtime>`, with a 15 s bound, and answers a `home_folder_list` frame carrying the listing or a reason (`outside_home`, `not_found`, `not_a_directory`, `invalid_path`, `unreadable`, `busy`, `disconnected`), each refusal logged as `add_project.node_refused` (`spawn_node_ask` in `hided/src/server.rs`).
The node opens the folder against its own home by the same file identity the registration line uses and lists it through a handle confined to home (`hide_host::browse`): a link that leaves home is no row, a `.` name or a file the system marks hidden is left out (`hide_platform::fs::hidden`), rows are capped at `LIST_CAP`, and each folder carries whether it is a repository, its branch, or how many repositories it holds directly (capped at 200 children a folder and 4000 for the answer). The badge is read through the handle on home alone: a linked worktree's `gitdir:` and `commondir` are placed against home from their text, and one whose Git folder or repository lies outside home gets no badge, with nothing there read; each Git file is opened without waiting for a writer and read only when the opened handle is a regular file, at most 4 KiB (`hide_host::list::open_regular_file`), so a FIFO at `.git/HEAD` costs that row its badge and holds no node worker.
On a device, `project_target` and `clone_target` are asked of that device's node the same way (`Call::NewFolderTarget`), and their frames carry `device_id`; for this machine hided answers them itself, and both judge a parent under home and one folder name with the one function, `hide_host::browse::new_folder_target` (`Boundary::resolve_new_project` and `resolve_clone_target` call it), so this machine and a device never answer the same folder differently.
Create new project names a folder that does not exist yet, so a `create_workspace` with `new_folder` is judged as a parent on the `$HOME` line (home itself allowed) and one folder name (`Boundary::resolve_new_project`), and refused as `already_exists` when anything other than an empty folder, or one holding only `.git` and `.DS_Store`, stands at the target (`hide_host::project::folder`, read without following a symlink); the canonical target is forwarded.
The same check answers a client's `project_target` probe as a `project_target` frame, which the dialog shows before anything is sent; the probe is never forwarded and changes nothing on disk.
Add a project's projects to import are an `importable_projects` {device_id} answered the same way: hided takes the paths of the core's registrations on that machine (`Core::registered_paths`, one owner-thread call) and asks that machine's node `Call::ImportableProjects` with them to leave out, with a 30 s bound; the node reads every agent's session walk (`SessionCatalog::worked_folders`, the walk the session archive reads, so a new session reader joins it, each agent's store on its own, under its own budget of `SESSION_DISCOVERY_LIMIT` entries, so one that cannot be listed, is past its budget or cannot be read takes no other with it, and the kept headers of each store listed whole are pruned to it; a session file that names no folder a session could be placed in, Hide's own label session, a subagent's or a headless run's, or a Cursor session whose folder cannot be confirmed, is skipped as work in no folder and is no refusal of its store, which the retirement of `~/hide` relies on to finish, while a store that cannot be listed, is past its budget or is out of time still refuses), Paseo's registry and Herdr's save, each capped, only read and opened only as a regular file without waiting (`hide_platform::fs::open_regular`, so a pipe there is refused at once), judges each folder by the registration rule (`hide_host::register::judge`), and answers at most twenty roots by its own 20 s deadline (`IMPORTABLE_SEARCH_BUDGET`, under hided's bound, a source not reached by then dropped as late, so no search outlives its ask), each source it could not read logged by hided as `add_project.import_source_dropped`. The list adds a row with a `create_workspace` carrying a `request_id`; the core keeps a receipt for it beside `hide <path>`'s, under the same bounds (`Runtime::await_add`: at most 32 waiting, and at most 32 settled with the oldest dropped first, so a refusal always has room; an add not admitted, with 32 waiting or a reused id, is kept as a receipt refused at once, `workspace.create_busy` or `workspace.create_refused`), settles every receipt waiting on that machine and path with the registration's outcome, and publishes the adds' receipts as `status.project_adds` (`pending`, `added`, or `refused` with the error's kind and message), which no later event clears; hided's `path_refused` names the id too, so a row reads only its own answer.
